findings.title: A stale poller snapshot can permanently discard a land trigger
findings.detail: When any saved PR snapshot exists, the land-trigger consumer uses it without refreshing GitHub. If that snapshot has the previous head, `startConflictTrigger` marks the new trigger skipped as `PR head moved`. The trigger is never reconsidered when the poller catches up, so the blocked land entry can remain unresolved indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: Refresh or defer a land trigger when the saved observation does not match its head, and retain it until a current observation can determine eligibility.
findings.failure_scenario: A PR head is updated and approved before the next GitHub poll. Landing finds a conflict at the approved head, but the saved snapshot still names the preceding head; the only land trigger is skipped.

findings.title: A conflict observed during another round is discarded permanently
findings.detail: An active review or conflict round causes the trigger to be marked skipped. If that round fails or finishes without resolving the newly observed conflict, neither the land queue nor the poller necessarily emits another trigger: the land entry is already blocked and mergeability remains CONFLICTING. The requested conflict round is therefore lost.
findings.suggestion: Keep the trigger pending while another round is active and reconsider it when that round ends, subject to a fresh head and eligibility check.
findings.failure_scenario: A review round is in flight when the base advances and the land queue blocks on a conflict. The trigger is skipped; the review round then fails its gates and the PR remains conflicting without a conflict round.

findings.title: Conflict rows change previous-release review-round accounting after rollback
findings.detail: The previous release reads every row in `review_rounds` as a review round and counts all of them toward its review-round cap. The migration preserves insert compatibility but adds conflict rows to that same table, so rolling back after conflict rounds have run can make an ordinary changes-requested review immediately put the owning run into needs-human with `review round limit reached`.
findings.suggestion: Keep conflict records outside the previous release's review-round view, or otherwise preserve its accounting across rollback.
findings.failure_scenario: The new release creates three completed conflict rounds for a PR, then deployment rolls back. A reviewer requests changes; the previous release counts those conflict rows against its review cap and refuses to create the requested review round.

findings.title: A transient PR lookup failure leaves a trigger pending without a retry
findings.detail: A failed lookup leaves the trigger pending, but the land queue invokes this consumer only at startup and after another land failure. If the PR has no usable poller snapshot, no later observation is guaranteed to consume it. A transient GitHub failure can therefore drop the requested work until an unrelated event or daemon restart.
findings.suggestion: Arrange a bounded retry or another durable wake-up for pending triggers after lookup failures.
findings.failure_scenario: A land conflict is recorded before the PR has a saved poller snapshot and `gh pr view` temporarily fails. The queue logs the error and remains running, while the blocked entry and pending trigger receive no further processing.

findings.title: A stale poller snapshot can permanently discard a land conflict trigger
findings.detail: When any saved snapshot exists, the trigger is decided from it without refreshing the PR. startConflictTrigger marks a rejected trigger skipped permanently. For example, a snapshot can still say draft after the PR has been made ready and approved; a land conflict then gets skipped as draft. A later poll that observes the same head as still conflicting need not emit another pr.conflicting transition, leaving the blocked entry without a round.
findings.suggestion: Refresh the PR observation for a land trigger before permanently rejecting it, or retain the trigger until a current observation can decide it.
findings.failure_scenario: The last poll saw a draft PR with a conflicting head. The PR becomes ready, is approved, and the land queue detects a conflict before the next poll. The saved draft snapshot causes the only land trigger to be skipped.

findings.title: Conflict rounds are indistinguishable from review rounds to a rolled-back release
findings.detail: The migration stores both kinds in review_rounds, but the previous release reads every row as a review round and counts them against the configured review-round budget. After rollback, a delivered or failed conflict round can therefore exhaust that budget and prevent a legitimate review follow-up; an in-flight conflict round is also treated as an ordinary review round on resume.
findings.suggestion: Keep conflict-round records separate from the table read by the previous release, or otherwise ensure the previous release cannot interpret them as review rounds.
findings.failure_scenario: With review_rounds set to 1, a conflict round is recorded, the daemon rolls back to the previous release, and a subsequent changes-requested review is refused because the old code counts the conflict round as the one permitted review round.

findings.title: Resumed retries reuse results after their build artifacts are removed
findings.detail: A completed initial attempt is returned from persisted gateResults on restart, but prepare discards worktree changes before reaching it, and the gates stage checks out the committed tree before reaching it. A pending local retry then runs without the setup and build outputs produced by the initial attempt. Previously, resuming the stage reran the initial suite and recreated those outputs before retrying.
findings.suggestion: For local executions, reconstruct the initial attempt and its required worktree state before resuming a retry, or otherwise ensure the retry has the same setup outputs as its first attempt.
findings.failure_scenario: A gate setup creates an untracked build directory, a check fails transiently, and the daemon restarts during its retry. On resume the directory is cleaned, the saved initial result is reused, and the retry fails because its build output is missing.

findings.title: Executor events are never consumed
findings.detail: executeGate awaits only execution.result and never reads execution.events. Local execution happens to invoke the caller's hooks directly, but an executor implementing the advertised interface has no access to those hooks. Its check and status events therefore never reach pipeline events or the landing log, so routing through the shared executor does not preserve gate event behavior.
findings.suggestion: Consume the execution event stream and forward events to the appropriate pipeline and landing reporting hooks, without duplicating local events.
findings.failure_scenario: An injected executor emits check events while a long gate suite runs. The run displays no per-check progress, and landing's log contains no check output even though the executor emitted it.

findings.title: Local start does not start an execution
findings.detail: start only allocates an ID and stores a signal; the actual gate work begins in attach. This contradicts the requested executor contract that start starts work and attach reattaches to already-started work. A caller using the interface independently cannot start work and later attach to its progress or result.
findings.suggestion: Start local work as part of start and have attach retrieve that execution, retaining the specified replay behavior for handles recovered after a restart.
findings.failure_scenario: A caller invokes local start and delays attach while doing other work. No gate command runs during that interval, and attach starts a new execution instead of attaching to one already running.

findings.title: Restarting a regression retry removes its required build output

findings.suggestion: Avoid granting file content access outside the requested allowlist, or restrict any necessary discovery exceptions so home files remain unreadable.
findings.failure_scenario: A gate runs cat on the owner's ~/bunfig.toml or ~/package.json; the generated literal allow overrides the home deny and exposes its contents.

findings.title: Cargo configuration credentials remain readable to gates
findings.detail: The gate allowlist explicitly exposes Cargo's config and config.toml, and runConfined also copies those files into readable scratch. Cargo configurations can contain registry tokens, including legacy registry.token and registries.<name>.token entries. Denying only Cargo's credentials files therefore does not keep every credential store outside the gate allowlist.
findings.suggestion: Do not expose or copy credential-bearing Cargo configuration to untrusted commands; provide only configuration that has been safely stripped of credentials.
findings.failure_scenario: An owner has a private registry token in ~/.cargo/config.toml. Candidate gate code reads that file directly or from $CARGO_HOME/config.toml and sends the token over HTTPS.

findings.title: A missed post-merge observation permanently leaves the merge feed incomplete

With polling disabled, the reconciliation path also deliberately does not fetch metadata for an already merged run, so the run fields can remain null indefinitely. This leaves the reported inconsistency unresolved after an ordinary transient lookup failure or daemon restart.

beta-secret-value"); console.log(redactCredentials("+alpha-secret-value
+beta-secret-value
"));'` printed both `+alpha-secret-value` and `+beta-secret-value` unchanged.

findings.title: Setup variants can make policy generation select the wrong evidence
findings.detail: Adding setup to the system identity allows an eval to contain both setup and non-setup standard systems for the same target. Policy generation accepts both as production-compatible, but takes only the first summary for that target. Consequently, the generated routing policy depends on systems-file ordering and can silently use the non-setup arm while ignoring the production-like setup arm.
findings.suggestion: Define which setup variant supplies routing evidence and select it explicitly, or reject ambiguous systems for policy generation.
findings.failure_scenario: An eval includes standard systems for the same model with and without setup, with the non-setup system listed first. Policy generation uses its results and ignores the setup system's results.

findings.title: Late exceptions are included in preparation time
findings.detail: Review trials never set roundsUsed, so an exception after the reviewer starts enters this branch and replaces the already recorded preparation time with elapsed time since preparation began. It also labels the invocation as a preparation failure. For example, an origin exclusion raised during invocation can make reviewer time appear as preparation time.
findings.suggestion: Track whether preparation completed separately and preserve its recorded duration after invocation begins.
findings.failure_scenario: A review invocation runs and then raises an OriginExcludedError; the recorded preparationMs includes the invocation and preparationFailed is true.

findings.title: Cached trials still require setup to succeed

findings.suggestion: Compute and check the trial's cache identity before running setup, and run setup only when the reviewer will actually be invoked.

findings.title: Keep unrelated patch lines visible when a credential matches

This fails the explicit acceptance criterion that the rest of the file remain visible, and can hide unrelated changes even when the credential itself is outside the displayed hunks. The new test asserts the whole-file marker instead of checking that public lines survive.

findings.failure_scenario: An added file contains public lines before and after a registered two-line credential. The response contains only '[withheld: private text; 1 file]', so neither public line is available.

findings.title: Protect multiline credentials in diffs embedded in reports
findings.detail:
Persisted reports are still checked as ordinary text, so a diff with a prefix on each credential line bypasses the literal matcher and can be returned in report pages. The request calls for other diff renderings to receive the same treatment or be listed as follow-ups; neither happened. The targeted command `bun -e 'import { privateMatches } from "./src/gates/private.ts"; const credential="alpha-secret
beta-secret"; const report="```diff
+alpha-secret
+beta-secret
```"; console.log(JSON.stringify({reportMatches: privateMatches(report,[{value:credential,entry:1}]).length, fileMatches: privateMatches("alpha-secret
beta-secret",[{value:credential,entry:1}]).length}));'` returned `{"reportMatches":0,"fileMatches":1}`.

findings.detail: A match anywhere in either complete file causes the entire patch to be replaced by a single withholding message. The request explicitly requires withholding the lines spanned by the match while keeping the rest of the file visible. The added test instead asserts that the entire file is withheld.

A small diff to a larger file therefore makes the entire change-view request fail, even when the diff itself is small and contains no credential.

findings.title: A passing retry can clear a security check failure
findings.detail: Classification treats every successful full retry as nonblocking flaky unless it is a confinement error. There is no corresponding protection for other security checks, despite the explicit requirement that their failures never become a pass.

findings.title: A passing retry can clear a security check failure
findings.detail: The retry classification applies to every regressed check without distinguishing security checks. A security check that fails initially and passes on the full retry becomes nonblocking and flaky, contrary to the explicit requirement that a security failure never become a pass. A direct call to retryRegressions with a check named security, a failing original result, and passing targeted and full retry results returned verdict "flaky" and blocking false.

findings.failure_scenario: A configured security check reports a vulnerability on its first execution but passes on retry; the factory treats the check as nonblocking.

findings.title: Failures pointing at changed files never receive the requested targeted retry
findings.detail: The existing output-location exclusion still removes a regression before its structured failing files are considered. Test failures commonly include a stack location in a changed test or source file, so these failures receive no targeted confirmation even when the JUnit report identifies their files. The request requires a known-file failure to receive a targeted retry.

output.summary: Reviewed the pairing, heartbeat, TLS and sandbox paths as the first split described in the request. The targeted command `bun test test/workers.test.ts` could not start because `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/index.js` is missing from the environment; it ran zero tests.

findings.title: Pairing code does not authenticate the coordinator certificate
findings.detail: The first request accepts any TLS certificate and pins its fingerprint. An active intermediary can relay the pairing request and the coordinator's code and secret unchanged, so the owner and worker see matching codes, then relay approval and capture the issued token. The worker subsequently pins the intermediary's certificate. The submitted worker fingerprint is only stored; it does not bind the exchange to the worker either.
findings.suggestion: Bind the owner-verified pairing code to the coordinator certificate and worker identity, and verify that binding before sending the claim secret or accepting the token.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker on the LAN proxies the initial pairing connection to the real coordinator. The owner compares the identical displayed codes and approves, after which the proxy obtains the worker token.

findings.title: Worker credentials are not denied to agents in other processes
findings.detail: Private-file protection is an in-memory registry. The worker registers its token and coordinator fingerprint only in the separate `limitless worker` process, while the daemon builds agent sandbox policies from its own registry. Consequently, an editor launched by a daemon on that machine can read these files under the default data directory. Likewise, a previously generated coordinator TLS key is not registered when the listener is disabled, although the key remains on disk.
findings.suggestion: Register the persistent worker credential paths and coordinator key in every daemon process before launching agents, including when the listener is disabled.
findings.failure_scenario: A machine runs both a paired worker and the factory daemon. A tool-enabled editor reads `<data>/worker/token` because only the worker process registered that path, exposing the bearer credential.

output.summary: Reviewed the pairing and heartbeat implementation and its credential lifecycle. Targeted tests could not load: the available dependencies lack @simplewebauthn/server and provide an incompatible Zod version.

findings.title: Worker credentials are protected only in the worker process
findings.detail: Private read protections are held in a process-local map. The worker CLI registers its token and coordinator fingerprint in its own process, so a separately running Limitless daemon on the same machine does not include those paths in its agent sandbox deny list. The same problem applies to a coordinator TLS key after its listener is disabled: the persisted key is no longer registered by the daemon. Tool-enabled editors can consequently read these files as the same OS user.
findings.suggestion: Register all persisted worker credential paths in each daemon before starting agents, regardless of whether the worker listener or worker CLI is running, and test across separate processes.
findings.failure_scenario: A machine is paired as a worker and also runs the factory daemon. An editor launched by that daemon reads the worker token from the data directory because the worker CLI's protection is invisible to the daemon.

findings.title: Interrupted certificate creation prevents subsequent daemon starts
findings.detail: Certificate creation publishes an empty key file before invoking openssl and never removes partial material on failure. A failed or interrupted first generation leaves either an empty key or an incomplete pair; later starts reject it or fail to parse it, and enabling the worker listener makes that failure abort daemon startup.
findings.suggestion: Generate the key and certificate under temporary names and publish them only after both are valid, cleaning up partial files on failure.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon stops or openssl fails after key.pem is created but before cert.pem is written. The next daemon start fails with incomplete worker TLS material until the files are manually repaired.

output.summary: Reviewed the pairing and heartbeat portion of the requested split. The targeted command `bun test test/workers.test.ts` could not run because the checkout is missing `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/index.js`; no test assertions ran.

findings.title: An interrupted approved pairing cannot be resumed
findings.detail: Once approval changes the row to `approved`, a new pairing request with the same name is rejected. If the worker loses its connection, exits, or fails to write its token after approval but before saving the credentials, it has no way to resume the claim: the claim secret exists only in the terminated process. Pairing again fails until the owner manually revokes the approved worker.
findings.suggestion: Provide a recovery path for an approved but unclaimed pairing, such as persisting the claim secret until the token is saved or allowing a securely authorized replacement request.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner approves a worker, then the network drops before the claim response reaches the worker. The worker command exits and a retry with the same name is refused as already paired.

findings.title: Failed certificate generation leaves unrecoverable partial material
findings.detail: Certificate generation creates the final key file before invoking OpenSSL, but the error path does not remove incomplete files. A failed or interrupted first generation leaves a key without a certificate, and every later start rejects the incomplete material instead of retrying.
findings.suggestion: Generate both files under temporary names and publish them together, or remove incomplete files when generation fails.
findings.failure_scenario: OpenSSL fails during the listener's first start after the empty key file is created. Subsequent daemon starts fail with `Incomplete worker TLS material` until the files are manually removed.

output.summary: Reviewed the pairing and heartbeat implementation as the first half of the permitted split. Targeted tests could not run because the checkout resolved missing or incompatible dependencies: @simplewebauthn/server was missing and the installed Zod lacked number().overwrite.

findings.title: Rollback leaves worker credentials readable by agents
findings.detail: The worker TLS key, worker token and pinned fingerprint are protected by registrations added only in the new daemon. After a rollback, the previous release does not register these paths, while the files remain on disk. Its agent read policy does not otherwise deny the worker directories, so a tool-enabled agent can read the retained private key or worker token.
findings.suggestion: Provide a rollback-compatible protection strategy before persisting these credentials, such as storing them under an existing credential directory that the previous release already denies.
findings.failure_scenario: A coordinator or worker is paired, a deployment rolls back to the previous release, and an agent running under that release reads the retained worker credential from the data directory.

findings.title: Interrupted certificate creation prevents subsequent startup
findings.detail: Certificate creation publishes an empty key file before running OpenSSL. If that process fails or the daemon is interrupted before the certificate is written, the next start sees incomplete TLS material and refuses to start; a partial certificate can likewise leave invalid material. Recovery requires manual removal of the files.
findings.suggestion: Generate both files under temporary names and publish them only after validating the completed pair, with recovery for an interrupted first creation.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon is stopped during its first certificate generation, leaving key.pem without cert.pem; every subsequent daemon start with workers enabled fails.

output.summary: Reviewed lease handling, worker execution, validation, fallback and restart paths. Targeted tests could not run because the checkout's dependencies are incomplete or incompatible: @simplewebauthn/server is missing and the installed Zod lacks number().overwrite.

findings.title: Restart discards durable jobs for gate retries
findings.detail: Only baseline, initial and rebase handles are eligible for reattachment. A shutdown during a timeout rerun or a baseline or regression retry leaves a durable LAN job, but the resumed run cancels it and enqueues another. This repeats gate work even if the worker completed and stored its result during the restart window, contrary to the requested restart behavior.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough retry state to reattach the matching LAN handle and consume its result after restart.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon shuts down while a regression-retry job is leased; the worker posts its result before the run resumes. The resumed run discards that completed job and runs the retry again.

findings.title: Fallback after restart uses the old baseline checkout path
findings.detail: The fallback runs the persisted request's cwd. A resumed prepare stage creates a new temporary baseline checkout, but the persisted request still names the previous checkout, which prepare removes during shutdown. If the reattached LAN job subsequently exhausts its attempts, local fallback runs against that obsolete path instead of the current checkout and fails.
findings.suggestion: Use the current attachment request's checkout for local fallback after verifying it represents the same requested commit.
findings.failure_scenario: Restart during a baseline LAN job, then let both worker attempts fail or expire. The local fallback uses the removed pre-restart baseline directory and the run fails instead of executing locally.

findings.title: Final result can contradict an already reported failing check
findings.detail: Check events and the final GateRun are validated independently. The coordinator accepts a failing check event followed by a passing final result for the same check, and grades the passing result. The worker result is explicitly untrusted, and this allows a reported failure to become a pass without being treated as an infrastructure failure.
findings.suggestion: Track the accepted check events for the active lease and reject a final result that contradicts them.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker posts a valid failure event for a requested check, then posts a structurally valid passing GateRun for that same check and SHA. The job is marked done with the passing result.

output.summary: Reviewed the LAN job lifecycle, result validation, worker execution, and restart paths. Targeted tests could not run because the checkout's installed dependencies were missing @simplewebauthn/server and had an incompatible Zod version.

findings.title: Verify the worker checkout HEAD after gates finish
findings.detail: The worker records HEAD before running the gate commands and posts that earlier value without checking HEAD again. A gate can change HEAD during execution, so the coordinator accepts a result for the requested SHA even though checks ran against a different commit. The coordinator's existing post-gate HEAD check only inspects its own checkout and cannot detect a change in the worker checkout.
findings.suggestion: Read and validate HEAD again after the gate run and reject the result as an infrastructure failure if it changed.
findings.failure_scenario: A configured setup or check command runs git checkout or git reset to another commit and the subsequent checks pass; the worker reports the original SHA and the coordinator accepts the pass.

findings.title: Reattach to in-flight LAN retry jobs after restart
findings.detail: The resume condition only accepts baseline, initial, and rebase purposes. A persisted LAN timeout rerun or regression retry is instead cancelled and enqueued again after a daemon restart, even if the worker is still executing it or has already completed it. This repeats work and violates the requested durable reattachment behavior.
findings.suggestion: Preserve and reattach to the persisted LAN handle for retry purposes when its stage, round, purpose, and SHA still match.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while a long regression retry is running. On resume, the pending job is cancelled and a new job is started for the same retry.

output.summary: Reviewed the land-check retry, logging and restart paths. The targeted retry tests passed. The land-queue tests could not load because @modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js is missing from the environment.

findings.title: Clear a stale flake reason when checks restart
findings.detail: A successful targeted retry writes the flake reason before the checked head is checkpointed. If the daemon restarts while the entry is still checking, the checks run again, but a clean result leaves the old reason in place. The log is also overwritten on restart, so a later landed entry can claim a flake that is no longer present in its log or associated with the final check run.
findings.suggestion: Reset the prior check attempt’s flake reason when beginning a fresh checking attempt, or persist the flake evidence with the checked head and retain its corresponding log.
findings.failure_scenario: A targeted retry passes, then the daemon stops before pushedSha is recorded. On resume, the full check passes cleanly and the entry lands with the previous `flaky:` reason despite the new log showing only the clean run.

output.summary: Reviewed the retry, logging, confinement, and restart paths. The targeted retry tests passed; the land-queue tests could not load because @modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js is missing.

findings.title: Restart can retain a flaky outcome while erasing its evidence
findings.detail: The flaky reason is persisted before the entry reaches the waiting_ci checkpoint. If the daemon restarts in that interval, checking runs again and overwrites the land log. A clean second check leaves the old flaky reason in place, so the entry can land as flaky even though its log no longer contains the first failure or targeted retry. This misses the requested record of both attempts.
findings.suggestion: Keep the flaky outcome and its log evidence consistent across a restart, for example by preserving prior attempt logs or clearing the stale outcome when restarting checks.
findings.failure_scenario: A targeted retry passes, then the daemon restarts during the subsequent private-range check or push, before pushedSha is checkpointed. On resume, the full checks pass cleanly; the log is replaced, but the existing flaky reason survives through landing.

output.summary: Reviewed the sandbox settings, verifier invocation path, and smoke probe. Targeted tests could not run because the checkout’s available dependencies lack Zod’s prefault method and @anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime.

findings.title: Allow the Bun executable the verifier will actually resolve
findings.detail: The allowance is derived from the daemon’s process.execPath, but a verifier runs `bun` through its shell PATH. Those can resolve to different installations, particularly when the daemon and interactive tool environments have different PATHs. If the shell’s Bun is under a denied private root, it remains unreadable and verification still cannot run tests.
findings.suggestion: Resolve the Bun executable using the environment passed to the verifier, validate its canonical path against credential denies, and allow that executable.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon runs with Homebrew Bun while the verifier’s PATH resolves `bun` to ~/.bun/bin/bun. The settings allow the Homebrew executable but deny the executable selected by the verifier.

findings.title: Exercise the verifier’s normal Bun command in the live check
findings.detail: The probe launches process.execPath directly, so it bypasses shell PATH resolution and always tests the same executable that the new settings explicitly allow. It can pass while the `bun test` command a verifier actually runs remains blocked. This leaves the requested live regression check unable to detect that failure.
findings.suggestion: Have the bounded probe execute `bun test` through the verifier’s normal command environment, while retaining the timeout and independently checked output.
findings.failure_scenario: The smoke process uses Homebrew Bun but the Claude shell resolves `bun` to a denied ~/.bun installation. The smoke check passes even though verifier test commands fail.

output.summary: Reviewed the Claude sandbox settings, verifier invocation, lease handling, and smoke probe. The focused test command could not run because the available dependencies lack Zod's prefault API and @anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime.

findings.title: Allow the Bun executable used by the verifier's shell
findings.detail: The read exception is derived from the daemon's process.execPath, but a verifier normally runs `bun test` through its shell and resolves `bun` from PATH. Those can be different installations. In that case the shell-selected executable remains under the home-wide read deny, so the reported hang or execution failure remains. The new smoke check also invokes process.execPath explicitly, so it can pass without exercising the executable the verifier would select.
findings.suggestion: Resolve and validate the Bun executable available to the verifier's actual shell environment, and have the live probe run `bun test` through that same resolution path.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon starts with one Bun installation while the verifier's PATH selects another installation under the user's home directory; the verifier runs `bun test`, but only the daemon's executable is allowlisted.

output.summary: Reviewed the publication paths and sanitizer. Targeted tests could not start because the checkout lacks the entities dependency; a standalone execution of the sanitizer exposed two path-handling defects.

findings.title: Encoded and file-URI paths bypass publication sanitization
findings.detail: The matcher recognizes only literal filesystem roots. A file URI or an HTML-entity-encoded path is left unchanged, so the published report can still expose the owner's username and factory layout. A standalone execution returned `[file](file:///factory/data/work/run/file.ts)` and `[file](/factory/data/work/run/file.ts)` unchanged. The private-string check may block some such reports once configured, but that still prevents the delivery this change is intended to permit.
findings.suggestion: Recognize and decode supported local URI and Markdown path representations before classifying them, then emit a sanitized representation.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer report links to `file:///Users/<user>/.limitless/work/<run>/test/example.ts`; the absolute local path remains in the PR body.

findings.title: Parent-directory components misclassify paths outside the worktree
findings.detail: The root check uses a textual prefix without resolving `..`. A standalone execution transformed `[file](/factory/data/work/run/../other/log.txt)` into `[../other/log.txt](../other/log.txt)`, treating a path outside the worktree as a repository file instead of replacing the factory data prefix with `<data>`. This also produces a broken GitHub link.
findings.suggestion: Normalize path components before determining whether the target is inside the worktree or elsewhere under the data directory.
findings.failure_scenario: A report refers to a neighboring run's log through `<worktree>/../other/log.txt`; publication emits a repository-relative link instead of a plain `<data>` path.

output.summary: Reviewed the publication rewrite and its delivery call sites. The targeted test could not run because the checkout lacks the entities dependency. Direct sanitizer probes exposed three path-handling defects.

findings.title: Absolute paths in link labels pass through unchanged
findings.detail: The link alternative consumes the entire Markdown link, but only its destination is inspected. If the destination is relative, the original link is returned even when its label contains an absolute worktree path. That can publish the owner's username and local layout. A direct sanitizer probe returned `[/factory/data/work/run/test.ts](test.ts)` unchanged.
findings.suggestion: Sanitize path-bearing link labels as well as destinations, including when the destination itself is already relative.
findings.failure_scenario: A report contains `[/Users/owner/.limitless/work/run/test.ts](test.ts)` and the private-string list does not yet contain the username; the PR publishes the absolute path.

findings.title: Home-relative and file-URL paths are not rewritten
findings.detail: Matching only the literal absolute roots leaves equivalent `~/.limitless/...` paths and `file:///...` destinations unchanged. The request explicitly gives home-relative worktree links as an example. A direct probe returned `[~/.limitless/work/run/test.ts](~/.limitless/work/run/test.ts)` unchanged; a file-URL probe also returned its input unchanged.
findings.suggestion: Recognize the supported home-relative and file-URL forms and resolve them against the configured roots before rewriting.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer reports `[test](~/.limitless/work/run/test.ts)` or `[test](file:///Users/owner/.limitless/work/run/test.ts)`; delivery leaves the broken local link in public text, and the latter can expose the local username.

findings.title: Traversal paths are classified before normalization
findings.detail: The prefix test treats paths containing `..` as inside the worktree even when they resolve outside it. A direct probe converted `[log](/factory/data/work/run/../other/log)` to `[../other/log](../other/log)` instead of the required plain `<data>` path.
findings.suggestion: Normalize path components before deciding whether the destination is inside the worktree or only inside the data directory.
findings.failure_scenario: A report links a sibling run's log through `<worktree>/../other/log`; the published report presents it as a repository-relative link rather than a data-directory placeholder.

output.summary: Reviewed claim ownership across the land queue, its Git helpers, and cleanup. The targeted land-queue test could not run because the checkout is missing @modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js.

findings.title: Recheck ownership inside the merge operation before issuing the command
findings.detail: The ownership check runs before calling mergePullRequest, but that helper awaits a GitHub PR lookup before issuing gh pr merge and can also await retry reconciliation. A reclaim during one of those awaits leaves the old signal live until its next heartbeat, so the old worker can still issue a merge after losing its claim.
findings.suggestion: Pass a claim-validity guard into the merge helper and check it immediately before every merge command, including retries.
findings.failure_scenario: The PR lookup inside mergePullRequest is deferred, another worker reclaims the entry, and the lookup returns before the old worker's heartbeat. The old worker then invokes gh pr merge.

findings.title: Recheck ownership immediately before the actual push
findings.detail: The claim is checked before calling pushExistingBranch, but that helper awaits commit resolution, transport setup, a remote lookup, and an ancestry check before issuing git push. Losing the claim during any of those awaits allows the old worker to push before its heartbeat detects the reclaim.
findings.suggestion: Provide the push helper with a claim-validity guard and check it immediately before issuing the push.
findings.failure_scenario: A land that needs a base merge pauses in pushExistingBranch's remote lookup; another worker reclaims the entry; the lookup completes before the heartbeat, and the old worker pushes its merge commit.

findings.title: Do not discard a reclaimed worker's shared checkout
findings.detail: The finally block unconditionally removes the checkout even when an ownership check detects a reclaim. Both attempts use the same land-<entry id> path, so the old worker can remove the new owner's checkout while that owner is using it. The early recovery path also discards this shared path after recording a merge.
findings.suggestion: Give attempts separate checkout paths or otherwise ensure cleanup cannot remove a checkout belonging to a newer claim.
findings.failure_scenario: A second daemon reclaims an entry and creates its checkout while the first worker is awaiting CI. The first worker detects the lost claim, enters finally, and removes the second worker's checkout, causing its checks or Git commands to fail.

output.summary: Reviewed claim checks and the surrounding land and GitHub paths. The targeted command `bun test test/land-queue.test.ts` could not run because the checkout lacks `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js`.

findings.title: Recheck ownership inside the merge operation before issuing the command
findings.detail: The ownership check happens before calling `mergePullRequest`, but that helper awaits a GitHub PR lookup before issuing `gh pr merge`. It can also await reconciliation and retry before another merge attempt. A reclaim during either await leaves the old worker's signal live until its next heartbeat, so it can still issue a merge after losing its claim.
findings.suggestion: Pass an ownership guard into the merge helper and check it immediately before each merge command, including retries.
findings.failure_scenario: The old worker enters `mergePullRequest`, its `gh pr view` is delayed, another owner reclaims the entry, and the view returns before the heartbeat; the old worker then runs `gh pr merge`.

findings.title: Do not discard the reclaimed worker's shared checkout
findings.detail: The `finally` block unconditionally removes the worktree at the path derived solely from the entry ID. After reclaim, the new worker uses that same path. If the old worker detects lost ownership and exits after the new worker has created its checkout, the old worker removes the new worker's files and Git worktree registration.
findings.suggestion: Make checkout cleanup safe across claim generations, for example by giving each claim its own worktree path and removing only that path.
findings.failure_scenario: A CI response is delayed, the entry is reclaimed and the new owner creates `land-<id>`, then the old response arrives and its claim check throws; the old worker's `finally` deletes the new checkout, causing its work to fail.

output.summary: Reviewed claim checks, land cleanup, CI rerun handling, and the changed tests. The targeted test command could not run because the checkout is missing the `entities` package.

findings.title: A refused rerun can remain pending after claim loss
findings.detail: The rerun is recorded as `rerun_requested` before the POST. If ownership changes while that POST is pending, the new guard discards its response. When GitHub refuses the request, no later workflow attempt exists to resolve the persisted pending record, so the replacement worker keeps waiting until the land times out instead of reporting the CI failure.
findings.suggestion: Give the replacement owner a way to reconcile an unresolved rerun request whose POST outcome was lost, without allowing the old owner to write after reclaim.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker claims a transient CI rerun, another owner reclaims the land while the rerun POST is in flight, and GitHub returns 422. The old worker discards the response; the new worker sees `rerun_requested` but the workflow attempt never advances.

output.summary: Reviewed claim validation, land checkpoints, merge and push guards, and CI inspection. The targeted tests could not run because the checkout is missing the `entities` package.

findings.title: A reclaimed entry can resume from a push that never happened
findings.detail: The worker records `pushedSha` before `pushExistingBranch` reaches its new ownership guard. If another worker reclaims the entry during the push helper's awaited remote checks, the guard prevents the push, but the replacement sees the recorded SHA and resumes as though it was published. When GitHub still reports the approved head, the replacement waits for CI on the unpublished SHA and eventually blocks instead of completing the land.
findings.suggestion: Reconcile the recorded SHA with the remote head on resume, and safely complete or retry the pending push when the remote still has the approved head.
findings.failure_scenario: The base advances, so landing creates a merge commit. The old worker stores that commit as `pushedSha`; a replacement reclaims the entry while the push helper awaits its remote lookup; the old worker's guard then refuses the push. The replacement waits for CI on a commit absent from the PR.

output.summary: Reviewed the runless request, persistence, restart, publication and display paths. The store tests passed. The queue test command could not run because the checkout lacks the @modelcontextprotocol/sdk client dependency.

findings.title: Bare PR numbers cannot request an unowned land
findings.detail: The documented `land <pr>` form accepts PR numbers for factory-owned entries, but the new path rejects every target that is not a full GitHub URL with `run not found`. The requested `limitless land <pr> --sha <full sha>` therefore does not work for an unowned PR when given its number.
findings.suggestion: Resolve a PR number against the configured repository context, and report a clear ambiguity if it cannot be resolved uniquely.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator runs `limitless land 599 --sha <current-full-sha>` for an open unowned PR; the request fails before consulting GitHub.

findings.title: Open fork PRs are excluded from the requested behavior
findings.detail: The request covers open PRs on a configured repository and does not exclude PRs whose head is in a fork. This unconditional rejection prevents those PRs from using the confined land checks.
findings.suggestion: Support the fork head with an appropriately pinned push and merge workflow, or explicitly obtain a narrower requirement.
findings.failure_scenario: A contributor opens a PR from a fork against a configured repository and the operator supplies its current full head SHA; the queue refuses it solely because `isCrossRepository` is true.

findings.title: Rollback blocks in-flight unowned lands
findings.detail: The empty-string sentinel satisfies the old schema, but the previous release treats it as a real run ID. After a rollback, its land worker calls `getRun("")`, throws `run  is gone`, and permanently blocks the entry. Thus an entry interrupted by a deploy cannot resume across the required previous-release compatibility window.
findings.suggestion: Use a compatibility strategy that prevents the old worker from claiming runless entries, or otherwise preserves their progress until a version that understands them resumes.
findings.failure_scenario: An unowned land is queued or waiting for CI when deployment rolls back to the base release; the old daemon claims it and changes it to blocked instead of resuming it.

findings.title: Unowned entries have no UI representation
findings.detail: The change emits feed records but adds no UI consumer for land entries. The existing UI has no `/api/land` consumer or land queue view, and its run detail refresh is keyed by a run ID, so a runless entry cannot appear there. The request explicitly requires the UI to show these entries.
findings.suggestion: Add a UI view or existing-screen integration that lists unowned entries and their current state.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator queues an unowned PR and opens the UI; neither its queued state nor a later blocked or landed state is shown.

output.summary: Reviewed the unowned PR path, persistence, restart behavior, and UI integration. The store tests passed. The queue tests could not load because @modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js is missing from this checkout.

findings.title: PR numbers cannot identify unowned pull requests
findings.detail: The CLI documents and accepts a PR number as a land target, but the new path accepts only a full GitHub URL. A numeric target with no matching factory run is rejected before GitHub is queried.
findings.suggestion: Resolve a PR number to a configured repository and canonical URL, with a clear ambiguity error when necessary.
findings.failure_scenario: `limitless land 599 --sha <current-full-sha>` returns `run not found` when PR 599 has no factory run.

findings.title: Fork pull requests are excluded from the requested support
findings.detail: The request covers open PRs on configured repositories without restricting their head repository. This unconditional rejection excludes normal contributor PRs opened from forks.
findings.suggestion: Support fetching and updating the PR's actual head repository while retaining the approved-SHA lease and publication checks.
findings.failure_scenario: An open PR targeting a configured repository from a contributor's fork is rejected with `cross-repository pull requests cannot be landed`.

findings.title: Rollback blocks active unowned lands
findings.detail: Unowned entries are persisted with an empty run ID. The previous release reads that value as a run ID and its land context requires a matching run, so after rollback it marks every active unowned entry blocked instead of resuming it. This violates the requested compatibility with the previous release and loses queued or in-progress work.
findings.suggestion: Provide a rollback-compatible representation or arrange for the older release to leave entries it cannot process intact.
findings.failure_scenario: An unowned land is waiting for CI when a deployment rolls back; the previous daemon claims it, fails to find run ``, and changes the entry to blocked.

findings.title: Unowned lands are not visible in the UI
findings.detail: The change adds API and feed records but no UI consumer for land entries. The UI displays runs and has no land queue view, so an entry without an owning run is not displayed there. The request explicitly requires these entries to appear in the UI.
findings.suggestion: Expose land entries in the UI, including their state and the absence of an owning run.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator queues an unowned PR and opens the UI: no run exists for it and no UI component renders its land entry.

output.summary: Reviewed cleanup persistence, recovery, and run resumption. The targeted command `bun test test/process-cleanup.test.ts` produced 8 passes and 3 failures because the checkout lacks `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js`; those startup and resume tests could not be verified in this environment.

findings.title: Recovery drops descendants that were not yet recorded
findings.detail: Recovery kills only the PIDs already in the table and then deletes the invocation's records. Live cleanup discovers processes over multiple scans: a descendant can fork after a snapshot and before its parent is frozen, or the daemon can crash partway through recording a snapshot. Such a descendant has no row, so recovery never discovers it and allows the next invocation to start while it continues running.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough invocation ownership information before cleanup begins to rediscover marked descendants during recovery, and complete the record only after the recovered set has been fully inspected and stopped.
findings.failure_scenario: A marked parent forks after the first scan; cleanup freezes the recorded parent, then the daemon crashes before the next scan records the child. Startup kills the parent, deletes the records, and leaves the child running in the checkout.

findings.title: A failed first ownership write leaves no durable block on the checkout
findings.detail: When the first ownership insert fails, the error path deliberately leaves the direct child alive. The termination error exists only in the current process scope, and no cleanup record exists for a later daemon or run to find. Once the storage failure clears, recovery sees an empty table and permits work to resume alongside the surviving process. The new test confirms the child remains alive but does not test recovery after the scope ends.
findings.suggestion: Create a durable invocation-level recovery record before starting the child, or otherwise ensure a failed ownership write leaves a durable block that prevents checkout reuse until cleanup is confirmed.
findings.failure_scenario: SQLite rejects the first cleanup insert during cancellation, for example because storage is temporarily full. The child remains alive; after restart and storage recovery, there is no pending row and a new invocation starts in the same checkout.

output.summary: Reviewed persistence, recovery, startup and resume paths. The targeted cleanup test ran 8 cases successfully; 3 could not run because the sandbox environment lacks @modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js.

findings.title: A crash during discovery leaves unrecorded descendants running
findings.detail: Members are recorded one at a time, and recovery only visits recorded PIDs. If the daemon dies after recording one member but before recording another member from the same scan, recovery kills the recorded member, deletes the record and allows the next invocation to start while the other descendant continues running. A descendant forked after the scan but before its parent is frozen is likewise absent from the record. This leaves an earlier invocation able to write to the checkout during resumed work.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough invocation ownership information before cleanup begins to rediscover and safely freeze descendants after a crash, and retain the record until a complete recovery sweep confirms that none remain.
findings.failure_scenario: An invocation has two marked sleepers. The daemon dies after persisting the first sleeper's identity but while awaiting the second's birth identity. On restart, recovery kills only the first sleeper and clears the invocation's records; the second sleeper remains alive as the run resumes.

output.summary: Reviewed the workflow, timeout wrapper, marker setup, and targeted tests. On macOS, the marker test passed and both Linux-only timeout tests were skipped, so the timeout behavior could not be exercised on its target platform.

findings.title: The inner timeout can expire after the job timeout
findings.detail: The 20-minute timer starts only after checkout, Bun setup, installation, and Git configuration, while the 25-minute limit covers the entire job. If those earlier steps take more than five minutes, GitHub can cancel the job before the wrapper prints its process tree or exits, recreating the missing-log problem.
findings.suggestion: Derive the check deadline from the job's start time, or otherwise reserve time for diagnostics within the outer job limit.
findings.failure_scenario: A slow dependency installation takes six minutes, then the test suite hangs. The job reaches its 25-minute limit after only 19 minutes in the wrapped check, before its 20-minute timeout fires.

output.summary: Reviewed the workflow, timeout helper, and test markers. The targeted test passed on macOS, but its two GNU timeout tests were skipped, so I could not run the helper’s Linux-specific checks here.

findings.title: Timeout cleanup leaves detached test children running
findings.detail: Cleanup sends signals only to the timeout process group. The test suite and subprocess utility create detached processes in separate groups, so those children do not receive either the monitor’s TERM or the final KILL. A surviving child can keep the step’s output pipe open and prevent the step from finishing before the outer job timeout, defeating the log-preservation change. The helper’s test covers only children in its own process group.
findings.suggestion: Terminate the descendant processes across process groups and add a timeout test with a detached child that inherits the output streams.
findings.failure_scenario: A test hangs while a detached subprocess created by src/util/proc.ts is still running and holding stdout or stderr open. The wrapper exits after its deadline, but the child survives and the CI step can remain open until GitHub cancels the job.

output.summary: Reviewed the audit, round-feedback, and publication-diagnostic paths. Targeted tests could not run because the checkout lacks the entities dependency; this was an environment limitation, not a test assertion failure.

findings.title: Warnings do not reach an implementer when the round otherwise passes
findings.detail: The advisory is added only when a later implementer invocation already occurs. If gates and review approve the first round, the pipeline proceeds toward publication without giving the implementer the warning or an opportunity to remove the scratch output. The new approve-case test explicitly expects only one implementer prompt.
findings.suggestion: Arrange an advisory follow-up that gives the implementer an opportunity to remove suspected scratch output while allowing intentional additions to proceed.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer adds .tmp-gate/report.xml, gates pass, and the reviewer approves. No subsequent implementer round receives the warning, so the report remains in the published history.

findings.title: Encoded credentials in diagnostic paths are not redacted
findings.detail: The new diagnostic applies literal credential redaction to the raw Git path. A credential with even one percent-encoded character does not match the registered literal, and private-string redaction does not protect registered credentials. The resulting error can store or display a recoverable credential.
findings.suggestion: Decode and sanitize path diagnostics before credential redaction, while handling paths that cannot be decoded safely.
findings.failure_scenario: A path contains a registered credential with its first character percent-encoded, and its content triggers the decoding refusal. The publication error includes the encoded credential in the reported path.

findings.title: Decoding refusals for empty-file paths lose their commit and path
findings.detail: The diagnostic maps patch sections to paths only through an index line. Git omits that line for an added or deleted empty file, so a decoding-limit refusal caused by its filename falls through to the original generic error. This misses the request to identify the commit and path responsible for a size refusal.
findings.suggestion: Associate patch sections with the raw diff records without requiring an index line, including empty-file additions and deletions.
findings.failure_scenario: A commit adds an empty file whose filename contains more than five nested percent-encoding layers. The aggregate scan refuses publication, but diagnosis finds no index line and reports only 'Published content exceeds the private text decoding limit'.

output.summary: Reviewed the audit, round feedback, and publication paths. Targeted tests could not start because the checkout lacks the entities dependency.

findings.title: Large text logs with control characters receive no size warning
findings.detail: The size map excludes every file that fails the stricter reviewable-text check, even when Git classifies it as text. That check rejects escape characters and other control bytes commonly present in terminal output. The audit then treats the missing size as zero, so a large log outside a root hidden directory receives neither requested advisory.
findings.suggestion: Record sizes for files classified as text independently of the stricter reviewable-text check, and cover a large log containing ANSI escape sequences.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer adds a 200 KiB root-level gate-output.txt containing ANSI color escapes. Git treats it as text, but reviewableText rejects the escape bytes, so large-text-addition does not warn.

output.summary: Reviewed the audit and publication redaction paths. Targeted tests could not run because the checkout lacks the entities dependency; a direct decoder probe ran successfully. The publication path still permits base64-encoded registered credentials to leave the factory.

findings.title: Publication checks do not receive registered credentials
findings.detail: The new base64 decoder only checks the entries passed by its caller. The production publication path passes privateEntries(), which contains private-strings.txt entries but not registered credentials. Its preceding redactCredentials() call removes literal credentials only. Consequently, base64-encoded credentials in PR text or the published commit range are not detected unless they also happen to be listed as private strings. The new test supplies credentials explicitly, unlike the production caller. A direct probe confirmed that privateMatches on an encoded registered credential with the production-equivalent empty private-entry list returns no matches.
findings.suggestion: Include registered credentials in the protected entries used by every publication check, including the commit range, and exercise the production caller in a test.
findings.failure_scenario: A report, PR comment, or committed file contains the standard base64 encoding of a registered credential that is absent from private-strings.txt; the publication check permits it and the encoded credential is published.

findings.title: URL-safe base64 runs bypass filename matching
findings.detail: The base64 run expression excludes '-' and '_', which are characters in the URL-safe base64 alphabet and are particularly suitable for filenames. A direct probe using the private entry 'private-slashed-entry???' and its URL-safe encoding 'cHJpdmF0ZS1zbGFzaGVkLWVudHJ5Pz8_' returned no matches. Such a filename can therefore remain in audit diagnostics.
findings.suggestion: Recognize URL-safe base64 runs as well as the standard alphabet, with a targeted filename test.
findings.failure_scenario: An audit finding names a file containing a URL-safe base64 encoding of a private entry or registered credential whose encoding includes '-' or '_'; the encoded value is stored and shown.

output.summary: The review found two credential-redaction bypasses. Targeted tests could not run because the checkout could not resolve the entities package.

findings.title: Publication checks do not include registered credentials
findings.detail: The new base64 decoder only searches the entries supplied by its caller. Production publication callers pass private-string entries, while registered credentials are only added for audit filenames and refusal diagnostics. Literal credential redaction does not remove their base64 encodings, so encoded credentials can still be published in PR text, commits, or changed content.
findings.suggestion: Include registered credentials in every publication check that handles outgoing text and content, and cover the production call paths with tests.
findings.failure_scenario: A registered credential absent from private-strings.txt appears base64-encoded in a changed file or PR body; the publication check accepts it and delivery exposes it.

findings.title: Base64 decoding stops before nested encodings can be inspected
findings.detail: A base64 run is decoded only when its immediate decoded bytes already contain a protected value. If those bytes contain a percent-encoded value, the run remains unchanged and the following decoding rounds never see the percent escapes. The same bypass applies to audit filenames and details. A targeted Bun probe encoding the percent-encoded value `synthetic-credential` returned `matches: []`.
findings.suggestion: Handle nested encodings without requiring the first base64-decoded layer to contain the final protected value, while retaining bounded decoding and false-positive controls.
findings.failure_scenario: A filename contains the base64 encoding of a percent-encoded registered credential; the audit persists and displays the encoded filename instead of replacing it with `[redacted filename]`.

output.summary: Reviewed the stored invocation, eval, CLI and HTTP paths. The provider workload tests passed. The CLI and HTTP tests could not complete because this checkout has missing or incompatible dependencies: the MCP SDK module was missing and the installed Zod lacked prefault.

findings.title: Eval trials are counted and attributed as individual provider calls
findings.detail: A trial or round can contain multiple actual calls. The eval runner combines panel finder and verifier calls, potentially across providers and models, into the trial's totals; it can also retry a failed resumed call within one round. This aggregation counts that combined work as one invocation and assigns all of its tokens and costs to the trial or round target. Successful share and per-provider/model workload are therefore wrong.
findings.suggestion: Aggregate actual persisted call-level evidence where available, and explicitly represent attribution or counts as unknown when the stored trial cannot support them.
findings.failure_scenario: A review panel uses provider A as its primary target and provider B as a verifier. Both calls are charged to A and the statistics report one invocation, with no workload for B.

findings.title: Completed multi-round evals lose their stored cache-token totals
findings.detail: Whenever a trial has rounds, the code sets both cache measurements to null for every round. The runner also persists aggregate cacheReadTokens and cacheWriteTokens on the trial, but these values are never used. Thus provider totals become unknown even for a single-provider trial whose cache totals are available.
findings.suggestion: Use the persisted trial cache totals when they can be attributed to a provider and model, while retaining unknown values where attribution is genuinely unavailable.
findings.failure_scenario: A completed implementation eval has two rounds on the same model and records cacheReadTokens and cacheWriteTokens in its details. Its provider and model totals report null for both cached-token metrics.

findings.title: Recorded work after the last completed round is dropped
findings.detail: Once details.rounds is nonempty, the aggregation ignores the trial-level totals entirely. The runner can persist additional spend and tokens while a later round is running, including after a failed session-resume attempt. If the daemon restarts before that round's evidence is appended, that recorded work remains in the trial totals but is permanently omitted from these statistics.
findings.suggestion: Account for persisted trial totals beyond completed round evidence, without double-counting completed rounds, and preserve unknown attribution when necessary.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementation eval completes round one, records usage from a failed resumed call in round two, and is interrupted before round two is appended. The reported workload includes only round one.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff and invocation-recording paths. The workload unit tests passed, but CLI and HTTP checks were blocked by incompatible or missing installed dependencies: Zod lacks prefault and the MCP SDK is absent. The eval aggregation has several material accuracy gaps.

findings.title: Eval trials are counted as individual provider invocations
findings.detail: A trial without implementation rounds is emitted as one invocation, although review panels, verifier calls and retries can make multiple provider calls, potentially using different models or providers. Their combined usage is attributed to the trial's provider and model, so both invocation counts and per-provider workload are wrong.
findings.suggestion: Aggregate individual recorded call evidence where available and explicitly represent cases where the persisted trial cannot support per-call attribution.
findings.failure_scenario: A review eval runs a finder and a verifier on different models; the result reports one invocation and attributes the combined spend and tokens to the trial model.

findings.title: Implementation evals discard recorded cache token totals
findings.detail: Every eval with recorded rounds forces cache-read and cache-write tokens to null, even when there is only one round and the trial records both values. Because a single null makes the aggregate null, one ordinary implementation eval also hides the provider's aggregate cached-token totals. The requested cached-token statistics are therefore unavailable for this normal eval path.
findings.suggestion: Use the stored trial cache totals when they can be attributed accurately, including single-round trials, and retain an explicit unknown only where a split cannot be recovered.
findings.failure_scenario: A single-round implementation eval records cacheReadTokens and cacheWriteTokens in its trial details; its model and provider cache totals are returned as null.

findings.title: Eval cutoff and day are based on trial creation rather than provider work
findings.detail: All rounds are filtered and grouped using the trial's creation time. A queued or long-running trial can execute rounds after the cutoff or on a later day, but those calls are excluded or assigned to the wrong day. This undermines both the since filter and daily workload numbers.
findings.suggestion: Use recorded call times for filtering and day grouping where available; expose the limitation where existing data cannot establish those times.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementation trial created before midnight performs a second provider round after midnight; a since cutoff at midnight excludes that round and the unfiltered report assigns it to the previous day.

findings.title: Implementation eval success share uses grading failures as invocation failures
findings.detail: The runner changes a round's recorded status to error or timeout when implementation grading fails or times out, even if the provider invocation itself returned ok. The aggregate treats that round status as the invocation status, so provider success share conflates provider failures with subsequent grading failures.
findings.suggestion: Use separately recorded invocation status when computing provider success, and avoid presenting grading status as provider-call success when the original status is unavailable.
findings.failure_scenario: A model invocation returns ok, but its implementation grading times out; the provider's successful share counts the invocation as failed.

output.summary: Reviewed signature selection, excerpts, rerun resolution, and credential redaction. The targeted test files could not load because the checkout is missing the entities package. A direct Bun probe reproduced a credential-redaction regression.

findings.title: Publication padding exposes short credentials in image values
findings.detail: Short registered credentials are redacted only when the entire input to redactCredentials equals the credential. publication passes surrounding log text as padding, so an image value that previously redacted as an exact match now remains visible and can be stored in the CI signature and emitted evidence. A direct probe with the same windowing logic produced {"old":"[redacted]","current":"abc123"} using: bun -e 'import {registerCredential,redactCredentials,credentialRedactionPadding} from "./src/util/proc.ts"; registerCredential("X", "abc123"); const text="prefix\nabc123\nsuffix"; const from=7, to=13, padding=credentialRedactionPadding(), start=Math.max(0,from-padding); console.log(JSON.stringify({old:redactCredentials(text.slice(from,to)),current:redactCredentials(text.slice(start,to+padding),{start:from-start,end:to-start})}));'
findings.suggestion: Preserve exact-window redaction for short credentials while retaining surrounding context for longer credentials, and cover the image-value path with a regression test.
findings.failure_scenario: A registered six-character credential is the value in a log line such as `Image: abc123`; the image field and signature contain `abc123` rather than `[redacted]`.

output.summary: Reviewed signature selection, excerpts, rerun reconciliation, and credential redaction. The targeted test files could not run because the checkout lacks the `entities` dependency.

findings.title: Windowed redaction can persist a short credential
findings.detail: For credentials shorter than eight characters, redaction only occurs when the entire input equals the credential. Windowed callers pass surrounding log text as input, so a selected line that exactly equals a short credential is no longer redacted. The resulting line and signature can be persisted in CI failure records. A targeted probe produced `old line: [redacted]` and `new window: error:` for the same registered credential.
findings.suggestion: Apply the existing exact-match rule to the selected window as well as the padded input, and test a short registered credential surrounded by other log lines.
findings.failure_scenario: A registered credential is `error:`, a CI log contains an `error:` line surrounded by other lines, and another registered credential supplies redaction padding. The signature line is stored as `error:` rather than `[redacted]`.

output.summary: Reviewed lease, checkout, event reporting, retry, and fencing paths. Targeted worker and agent-test suites could not run because installed dependencies are missing or incompatible: the worker suite could not find the MCP SDK, and the agent-test suite encountered a Zod version without prefault.

findings.title: Event sequence numbers restart on each attempt
findings.detail: Each worker attempt starts at sequence zero, but agent_job_events is keyed by job ID and sequence and silently ignores conflicts. Events persisted by a failed attempt therefore occupy the sequence numbers used by the next attempt, so the next attempt can complete with its early events missing and stale events from the failed attempt retained.
findings.suggestion: Make event storage attempt-aware or establish a durable sequence and clear separation between attempts.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker posts batch 0 and then loses its lease; a second worker runs the requeued job and posts batch 0, which is silently discarded before the job completes.

findings.title: Previously queued requests without a branch cannot run
findings.detail: The newly added branch field is optional on the persisted request, but the worker rejects every request that lacks it. Jobs queued by the previous release use the old request shape and consequently fail rather than running after an upgrade.
findings.suggestion: Provide a compatible branch value for old requests or otherwise migrate or handle the previous request shape.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent job queued before deployment contains the original request fields and no branch; after deployment, each worker rejects it with Missing or invalid agent branch.

findings.title: Fencing can run nearly a heartbeat interval after lease expiry
findings.detail: The interval only samples the elapsed time and uses a strict greater-than comparison. With the default 60-second lease and 10-second heartbeat interval, a partitioned session can continue for almost 70 seconds after the last successful heartbeat, including after the coordinator is entitled to reassign the job. This does not meet the requested one-lease-period fence.
findings.suggestion: Schedule or reset a deadline directly from each successful heartbeat and abort held agent jobs when that deadline expires.
findings.failure_scenario: Heartbeats stop succeeding just after a successful reply; the coordinator expires and reassigns the lease at 60 seconds while the original worker may continue its harness until the next interval tick.

output.summary: Reviewed the worker lifecycle, event reporting, fencing, checkout, and coordinator interactions. The targeted command `bun test test/workers.test.ts` could not run because the checkout lacks the `entities` package; Bun reported `Cannot find package 'entities' from 'src/gates/private.ts'` before running tests.

findings.title: Event sequence numbers collide across job attempts
findings.detail: Each worker attempt starts its event sequence at zero, but the coordinator stores batches under the primary key `(job_id, seq)` and silently ignores conflicts. If an attempt posts events and then fails, a subsequent worker's batches with the same sequence numbers are discarded, even if that worker completes the job. The persisted event stream can therefore describe the failed attempt while omitting events from the successful one.
findings.suggestion: Give each attempt a distinct event namespace or coordinate the next sequence number with the persisted stream, and test a retry after an attempt has posted events.
findings.failure_scenario: Worker A posts batch 0 and fails; worker B leases the same job, posts its own batch 0, and completes. The coordinator retains A's batch and silently drops B's batch.

findings.title: A rejected event batch aborts without reporting failure
findings.detail: A rejected batch aborts the job controller. The catch block then sees the aborted job signal and skips the failure POST. The coordinator continues to hold the lease until it expires or the worker becomes stale, delaying retry and leaving the job reported as leased after the session has stopped.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish an event-post failure from cancellation and fencing, abort the harness, and report the failure using a signal that remains usable for that notification.
findings.failure_scenario: The events endpoint rejects a batch with HTTP 400 while the worker and coordinator remain connected. The harness is aborted, but no failure is posted and the job remains leased until the coordinator's expiry sweep.

findings.title: Periodic fencing can leave an agent running beyond one lease period
findings.detail: The fence checks only once per heartbeat interval and uses a strict greater-than comparison. With the default 60-second lease and 10-second interval, a partition just after a successful heartbeat can leave the session running for nearly 70 seconds. The coordinator may already have expired and reassigned the job while the original worker continues spending quota.
findings.suggestion: Schedule fencing against the exact deadline derived from the last successful heartbeat, resetting that deadline on each success.
findings.failure_scenario: A heartbeat succeeds just after a fence tick and all later heartbeats fail. The check immediately before the 60-second deadline does nothing, and the next check does not abort the session until nearly 10 seconds after the deadline.

output.summary: Reviewed restart reconciliation, lease handling, adoption, and worker reporting. The targeted tests could not start because the checkout is missing the entities dependency.

findings.title: Check the remote before falling back after cancelling a dirty job
findings.detail: When re-attachment fails, the executor cancels the open job and calls prepare(). If the worktree is dirty, prepare() returns null before checking the remote branch, so the executor runs locally even if the worker already pushed a commit without an accepted report. This bypasses the required NeedsHuman outcome and can continue implementation with an unaccounted remote commit.
findings.suggestion: After cancelling an open job, check its remote branch against the stored expected SHA before any local fallback, including when prepare() declines a dirty worktree.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker pushes W but has not reported it when the coordinator restarts. The coordinator worktree is dirty, so resume() rejects the job; prepare() returns null without inspecting the branch, and a local session starts instead of ending NeedsHuman.

output.summary: Reviewed the restart, reconciliation, adoption, lease-grace, and worker-reporting paths. No definite defects were found. Targeted tests could not run because the checkout is missing the 'entities' dependency.
Reviewed worker dispatch, result validation, fallback, cancellation, and version-skew paths. Targeted tests could not start because the checkout lacks the entities dependency; no test assertions ran.

findings.title: Local panel finders can be dispatched to workers
findings.detail: Every production review call receives checkout metadata, including calls for finders marked local. The executor does not receive the finder’s local flag and only excludes targets with backend, openai, or decisions fields. A local finder routed to a Claude or Codex CLI target without those fields therefore becomes eligible for a worker, contrary to the explicit requirement that local finders stay local.
