findings.title: Coordinator confirmation discards the slow re-check history
findings.detail: When a slow regression is re-checked and fails, then receives coordinator confirmation, observationHistory returns only the confirmation outcome. The persisted observation retains slow_regression but has no record that the re-check failed. The request explicitly requires the combined retry_failed and confirmation history to remain evidence.
findings.suggestion: Persist the re-check outcome alongside the confirmation outcome, and classify confirmed passes by OS while retaining both pieces of history.
findings.failure_scenario: A Linux worker's slow regression fails its re-check, then passes confirmation on macOS. The observation is classified platform but records only confirmed_passed, losing retry_failed.

output.summary: Reviewed the lease manager against the claim client, time predicates, and durable intent recovery. The targeted command `bun test test/leases.test.ts` could not load the suite: the installed Zod throws `TypeError: floors.prefault is not a function` from `src/evals/settings.ts:14`. The findings below are based on the code paths inspected.

findings.title: Renewal loop omits recovered confirmed leases
findings.detail: The loop iterates only the in-memory `handles` map, which is populated after an applied write in this manager instance. Construction and intent reconciliation can leave confirmed held rows in the store without adding handles, so starting a manager after a daemon restart does not renew those leases. The same problem affects an acquisition that returns unconfirmed and is later confirmed by the loop.
findings.suggestion: Reconstruct eligible handles from confirmed held rows after recovery and reconciliation, or enumerate those rows on each tick.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts with a confirmed held lease and starts the manager. No new write populates `handles`, so subsequent ticks never renew it and the lease expires despite the active hook.

findings.title: Release intent replay bypasses lease-time validation
findings.detail: `reconcileLeaseIntent` replays a pending release whose tip is unchanged by calling `client.write` without a `beforeSend` predicate. Calling it here and during startup therefore permits a same-generation release after the lease window has closed and the generation has expired, without a fresh GitHub-time sample or send-time revalidation.
findings.suggestion: Ensure release replay uses the same fresh time decision and before-send revalidation as other same-generation writes.
findings.failure_scenario: A release is interrupted before its ref update, the daemon remains down past expiry, and recovery replays the release against the unchanged held tip. The expired generation changes the ref despite no longer being renewable.

findings.title: Startup recovery leaves dropped first acquisitions blocking other runs
findings.detail: The startup path calls `recoverLeases` directly, but unlike the local `reconcile` wrapper it does not forget a row when recovery drops an unconfirmed first acquisition. The resulting row has no intent and no confirmed ownership, yet belongs to the old run; a later run reaches `forgetLease` only after reading the ref, and an unresolved cross-run intent is refused before reconciliation. In particular, a pending intent from another run is never reconciled by that acquire operation, contrary to the required wait-and-reconcile behavior.
findings.suggestion: Apply the same dropped-row cleanup during startup and reconcile pending intents before deciding whether a different run is refused.
findings.failure_scenario: Run A leaves a pending first-acquisition intent and run B attempts acquisition while GitHub is temporarily unreadable. B receives `refused: live` without reconciling the intent, instead of `wait`; if B treats refusal as final, it cannot acquire after the uncertainty clears.

output.summary: Reviewed the lease manager against the claim client, durable intent recovery, and time predicates. The targeted command `bun test test/leases.test.ts` could not load the tests because the installed Zod lacks `prefault` (`TypeError: floors.prefault is not a function` in src/evals/settings.ts:14); no lease assertions ran.

findings.title: Renewal loop omits recovered confirmed leases
findings.detail: The loop iterates only the in-memory handles map, which is populated after a write returns applied in this manager instance. Creating a manager over a store with an already confirmed held lease, or reconciling an unconfirmed first acquisition to applied, never adds that lease to the map. The loop therefore never renews it even when the active hook would accept it.
findings.suggestion: Populate or derive renewal handles from confirmed held rows, including rows confirmed during reconciliation.
findings.failure_scenario: A daemon restarts with a confirmed held row and starts the manager without another successful acquisition write. Subsequent ticks do not renew the lease, which expires despite an active run.

findings.title: Release intent replay bypasses lease-time revalidation
findings.detail: Reconciliation delegates pending releases to reconcileLeaseIntent, whose replay calls client.write without a beforeSend hook or a GitHub-time decision. Consequently this manager can send a same-generation release after the lease has expired, including during startup recovery. The request requires every same-generation write to be revalidated immediately before sending.
findings.suggestion: Apply the same fresh-time decision and beforeSend predicate to release replays, leaving the intent unresolved when safe replay cannot be confirmed.
findings.failure_scenario: A release intent is persisted before its ref update, the daemon is down for more than ten minutes, and recovery finds the old held tip unchanged. Recovery writes the expired generation's release without checking renewable.

findings.title: Cross-run acquisition refuses before reconciling a pending intent
findings.detail: The different-run guard returns refused whenever the existing row has an intent, before reconciliation can determine whether that intent was dropped or remains pending. This violates the required pending-intent-first behavior and can prevent a subsequent run from acquiring a ref after an uncertain first acquisition.
findings.suggestion: Reconcile the row first, return wait while it remains pending, and only then apply the different-run ownership guard.
findings.failure_scenario: Run A's first acquisition returns unconfirmed but did not move the absent ref. Run B calls acquire before a renewal-loop tick: it receives refused without reconciling and forgetting A's never-confirmed row.

output.summary: Reviewed the browser verdict, preview, invocation, and resume paths. Focused tests could not start because the available dependencies lack `entities` and provide an incompatible Zod version.

findings.title: Treating absence of a warning as successful browser setup misclassifies failures
findings.detail: The engine records the browser as available whenever the preview is ready and this invocation has no `browser_unavailable` event. That event is emitted when browser configuration fails, but configuring MCP arguments does not establish that the MCP server connected or that Chromium started successfully. An MCP startup or browser launch failure after configuration can therefore produce no such event. A verifier that correctly reports the browser check blocked will instead have its result converted to unclear, causing product feedback rounds rather than the required bounded environment-block handling.
findings.suggestion: Record and persist affirmative, same-invocation evidence that browser setup succeeded, and classify missing or failed setup as unavailable or unknown rather than available.
findings.failure_scenario: A preview starts successfully, the browser configuration passes validation, but the MCP server or Chromium fails to start. The verifier reports a marked browser check as blocked; the engine records `available` and converts it to `unclear`.

output.summary: Reviewed the verification, preview, harness, and resume paths. The targeted tests could not run because the checkout is missing the entities package.

findings.title: Absence of a warning is treated as successful browser setup
findings.detail: The engine labels the browser available whenever the preview exists and the invocation has no browser_unavailable event. That event only reports failures while constructing the MCP configuration; it does not establish that the MCP server or Chromium actually started successfully. A verifier can therefore truthfully report a browser infrastructure failure, yet the engine converts its blocked row to unclear and sends it into an implementation feedback round.
findings.suggestion: Record a positive, same-invocation browser setup outcome and only convert blocked rows when that outcome confirms successful setup. Treat missing confirmation as unavailable or unknown.
findings.failure_scenario: A preview starts and browserMcp produces a configuration, but the configured MCP process fails to launch or initialize. No browser_unavailable event is emitted, so a marked browser check reported as blocked is converted to unclear and the run spends a feedback round on an infrastructure limitation.

output.summary: Reviewed lifecycle checkpoint recovery, publication inspection, label selection, and answer-command dispatch. The targeted command `bun test test/issue-queue.test.ts` could not run because the environment lacks `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js`.

findings.title: Recover uncertain posts before closing a suppressed checkpoint
findings.detail: The pending body is inspected before marker recovery. If inspection now fails, the checkpoint is marked done without checking whether GitHub accepted the earlier POST. This loses the durable record of an already-issued effect and violates the requirement to recover an uncertain POST by its marker before closing its checkpoint.
findings.suggestion: For checkpoints with a recovery page, search for the independently generated marker and checkpointed author before closing the effect. Apply current publication inspection before any subsequent POST.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub accepts a question comment but the response is lost. Before the next poll, private-string inspection becomes unavailable or its configuration changes so the stored body fails inspection. The next poll marks the effect done without finding and recording the accepted comment.

output.summary: Reviewed lifecycle publication, recovery, label selection, and answer-command dispatch. The targeted command `bun test test/issue-queue.test.ts` could not run because the checkout lacks `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js`; it failed during module loading before executing tests.

findings.title: A superseded question set can never be published if it becomes current again
findings.detail: Supersession marks the set's effect done even when no comment was posted. If the run later returns to waiting with the same unanswered IDs, observe sees the existing effect and will not create another publication. The recovery-pause test also expects this permanent closure.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish a published or suppressed set from an unsent superseded attempt, and permit a new attempt when that set becomes current again without reposting a recovered publication.
findings.failure_scenario: A run has unanswered question 42, leaves waiting while its publication is pending, and then returns to waiting with question 42 still open. The question remains unpublished on GitHub indefinitely.

findings.title: Needs-human comments remain eligible after the run resumes
findings.detail: The pre-POST eligibility check verifies the current status only for question effects. A pending needs-human comment can therefore be posted after the run leaves needs_human during identity lookup or recovery, presenting an obsolete reason as a current request for attention.
findings.suggestion: Recheck that a needs-human publication is still applicable immediately before posting and after awaited recovery or identity calls.
findings.failure_scenario: A needs-human comment waits on the GitHub identity lookup while a user resumes the run. Once lookup returns, the old needs-you comment is posted even though the run is running.

findings.title: Inspection failure closes an uncertain POST before marker recovery
findings.detail: An effect with a recovery page is marked done when reinspection of its stored body fails, before querying GitHub for the checkpointed marker. This violates the explicit requirement to recover an uncertain prior POST before closing its checkpoint.
findings.suggestion: Recover uncertain POSTs using the independently generated marker and checkpointed identity before closing the effect; suppress any new POST if current body inspection fails.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub accepts a question comment but the response is lost. Before the next poll, the private-string configuration changes or inspection becomes unavailable. The next poll closes the effect without checking whether GitHub accepted it.

output.summary: Reviewed the routing, explicit selection, eval, UI, and smoke-check changes. The targeted router and smoke test command could not complete cleanly because the installed Zod lacks APIs required by the existing code: `floors.prefault is not a function` and `z.number().overwrite is not a function`. The router tests otherwise reported 80 passes. Two defects remain in exclusion handling and reporting.

findings.title: An entirely excluded native provider fails deployment smoke checks
findings.detail: Native smoke checks call `cheapestModel`, which throws when every model for the provider is excluded. The smoke runner records those throws as failures, so `limitless deploy --smoke` fails even when the exclusion is intentional. Backend checks handle the equivalent condition as a skip. The new native smoke test checks the reason but does not check the failing statuses or exit code.
findings.suggestion: Mark native checks as skipped when the provider has no origin-eligible models, and assert that the smoke exit code remains successful for that case.
findings.failure_scenario: Configure `exclude_origins = ["US"]` with the default Claude and Codex catalogs, then deploy with `--smoke`: all native models are excluded and their smoke checks fail rather than skip.

findings.title: Verifier exhaustion can omit the required origin-exclusion reason
findings.detail: The exclusion reasons are reported only when every listed verifier is excluded. If an allowed verifier remains but shares a checkpoint with a finder that raised the candidate, `pickVerifier` rejects it and reports only that the verifier raised a candidate. The excluded independent verifier is absent from the error, although its exclusion is what leaves no usable verifier.
findings.suggestion: Include the collected origin-exclusion reasons when verifier selection fails after filtering, including when remaining targets are ineligible because they raised the candidate.
findings.failure_scenario: A panel has two verifier targets: an allowed model that raised the finding and an independent CN-origin model. With CN excluded, verification fails with only `verifier ... raised a candidate it would check`, without the required origin-excluded reason.

findings.title: Executable text remains blocked by the new byte classifier
findings.detail: The request limits the mode condition to inert-media paths, but this condition also applies it to any executable file that is not strict UTF-8 or contains certain control bytes. Git treats NUL-free files as text even when they contain, for example, a literal escape character or a byte in a legacy encoding. Such scripts are still reported as binary content and require an allowance, contrary to the requested behavior.
findings.suggestion: Apply the mode condition only to INERT_MEDIA_PATH matches, leaving the existing content classification to handle other paths.
findings.failure_scenario: An existing executable shell script contains a literal ESC byte in a printf string and is edited. Git displays its text diff, but reviewableText returns false and binaryPaths includes the script.

findings.title: Executable text is still blocked when it is not strict UTF-8
findings.detail: The new reviewableText check rejects invalid UTF-8 and several control bytes, although Git treats files without NUL bytes as text. Consequently, editing an executable script containing a Latin-1 comment or an escape byte still requires Allow: binary, contrary to the request that executable text be reviewed as text. A focused reproduction produced `1\t1\tscript.sh` from `git diff --numstat` and `["script.sh"]` from `diffSince` for a script containing a Latin-1 é.
findings.suggestion: Limit the executable-mode allowance condition to INERT_MEDIA_PATH as requested, leaving existing binary classification to determine whether other paths require an allowance.
findings.failure_scenario: An executable shell script contains `# café` encoded in Latin-1 and a later commit edits an echo statement. Git emits a text diff, but the audit flags the script as binary and blocks the run.

findings.title: A head change observed before draft deferral is recorded is never rechecked
findings.detail: Rechecking for a changed head depends on comparing the snapshot with the previously saved poller snapshot. Trigger processing also runs outside the poller and can record a draft deferral after the poller has already saved the new head. Subsequent observations of that still-draft PR have the same head, so this condition never calls the store's comparison against the trigger's observed SHA. The deferral remains skipped until some other qualifying change, contrary to the requested head-change recheck.
findings.suggestion: Evaluate draft deferrals against each observed snapshot, letting the store compare the snapshot head with each trigger's observed SHA; add a test where the poller saves the new head before the old-head trigger becomes draft-deferred.
findings.failure_scenario: A land trigger for head A is being processed while the poller observes and saves draft head B. The live lookup then records the trigger as skipped because the PR is a draft. Later polls continue to see draft head B, so the trigger is never rechecked for the head change.

findings.title: Consume land triggers using potentially stale PR observations
findings.detail: Any saved poller snapshot is treated as current and causes the trigger to be permanently started or skipped without a fresh lookup. A snapshot from before the PR head changed can make a valid land-conflict trigger skip as “PR head moved”; later polling does not restore that consumed trigger. Conversely, a snapshot from before a PR became draft can start a conflict round for that draft. The store also prefers the saved snapshot over the supplied observation.
findings.suggestion: Validate the trigger against a fresh PR observation, or keep it pending until the poller supplies a current observation; do not permanently skip it based on stale cached state.
findings.failure_scenario: The poller last observed head A, then a review round pushes head B. Before the next poll, landing B encounters a base conflict. The land trigger records B but is skipped against cached head A, leaving the entry blocked without starting the required resolution.

findings.title: Conflict rows change previous-release review-round accounting
findings.detail: The migration stores conflict rounds in the existing review_rounds table. After rollback, the previous release reads every row as a normal review round and counts it against the review-round cap. A delivered or failed conflict round can therefore make a subsequent changes-requested review immediately mark the owning run needs_human instead of starting its permitted review round. The default column value makes old inserts work but does not preserve old readers' behavior.
findings.suggestion: Keep conflict-round records invisible to the previous release's review-round queries, for example with separate storage and compatible new-release queries.
findings.failure_scenario: A PR with a review-round cap of one completes its first conflict round, then the deployment rolls back. A reviewer requests changes; the previous release sees one existing review round and refuses to start the actual review round.

findings.title: A stale poller snapshot can permanently discard a land trigger
findings.detail: When any saved snapshot exists, trigger processing uses it without refreshing the PR. `startConflictTrigger` marks a head mismatch as skipped. If the land queue observes and approves a newer head before the poller refreshes its snapshot, the conflict trigger is discarded; a later poll cannot consume it because it is no longer pending.
findings.suggestion: Refresh or wait for a current observation before deciding that a land trigger is ineligible; do not permanently skip it based on an older saved head.
findings.failure_scenario: The poller has saved head A, the PR advances to B, and the land queue approves B and blocks on a conflict before the next poll. Processing compares B with saved A and skips the only land trigger.

findings.title: Transient lookup failures can leave a durable trigger pending indefinitely
findings.detail: A failed PR lookup leaves the trigger pending, but the land queue processes pending triggers only at startup or after another land entry fails. The poller can consume it only if the PR has a saved snapshot or is subsequently observed. Thus a transient GitHub failure on a land trigger with no tracked snapshot can leave the requested round unstarted until an unrelated event or restart.
findings.suggestion: Schedule bounded retries for pending triggers independently of unrelated land failures, retaining the durable pending record until processing succeeds.
findings.failure_scenario: A land entry conflicts before the poller has saved its PR, and the one `gh pr view` lookup fails transiently. No other land operation fails and the PR is not tracked by the poller; the trigger remains pending indefinitely.

findings.title: Conflict rounds break review-round behavior after rollback
findings.detail: The migration stores conflict and review rounds together in `review_rounds`. The previous release reads all rows as ordinary review rounds and counts them against the review-round limit. After rollback, a completed conflict round can therefore cause an otherwise eligible review request to mark the owner needs-human rather than start a review round. An in-flight conflict round is also resumed by the old engine as an ordinary review round.
findings.suggestion: Keep conflict metadata and records in a form the previous release does not interpret as ordinary review rounds, and provide a safe rollback path for in-flight conflict runs.
findings.failure_scenario: A PR has a completed conflict round and a review-round cap of one. The daemon rolls back to the previous release, then receives changes requested on the PR; the old code counts the conflict row and refuses the review round.

findings.title: Restarting a retry reuses results after deleting its build output
findings.detail: Completed attempts are reused from state, but stage resume cleans the checkout before reaching this return. If the initial gate produced build output needed by a retry, that output is gone and the initial gate is not rerun to recreate it. The retry can therefore produce a different baseline or regression verdict after a restart.
findings.suggestion: Restore the inputs needed by a resumed local retry, or rerun the preceding local attempt when its checkout side effects cannot be preserved.
findings.failure_scenario: A setup command builds an ignored output directory, a check fails transiently, and the daemon restarts during its retry. On resume the checkout is cleaned, the saved initial result is reused, and the retry runs without the build output.

findings.title: Landing executions have no durable handle
findings.detail: The landing path calls executeGate without a persistence callback or stored handle. A daemon restart during a landing check therefore starts a new execution instead of attaching to the existing one. This leaves the landing path outside the requested durable executor lifecycle and can duplicate work for an executor whose work survives the daemon.
findings.suggestion: Persist the landing execution handle with the queue state and attach to it when the check resumes.
findings.failure_scenario: A landing check has started on an executor that survives daemon restarts; the daemon restarts before its result arrives, and the queue starts the same check again.

findings.title: Local start does not start an execution
findings.detail: Local start only allocates an ID and records the signal; the gate work begins in attach. Thus a handle returned by start does not identify work already started, contrary to the requested executor contract. A caller that starts work and delays attachment cannot rely on execution having begun.
findings.suggestion: Make start initiate the local execution and retain it for attach, while preserving replay for handles recovered after restart.
findings.failure_scenario: A caller awaits local start and persists its handle, but is interrupted or delays before attach; no gate work has started despite receiving a started execution handle.

findings.title: Executor events are never consumed
findings.detail: executeGate waits only for execution.result and never reads execution.events. Local executions happen to invoke the separately supplied hooks, but an executor that reports check events through the interface cannot populate pipeline gate events or landing logs. The shared executor path therefore loses the requested event behavior for such implementations.
findings.suggestion: Consume execution.events in the shared path and forward them to the appropriate gate event and logging hooks.
findings.failure_scenario: An injected executor emits check events and eventually returns a GateRun; the stage reaches a verdict, but its per-check events and landing log output are absent.

findings.title: Restarting a retry removes the setup artifacts it needs

findings.title: Landing executions have no durable handle
findings.detail: Landing calls executeGate without a persistence callback or stored handle. A restart while an executor is running therefore loses its handle and starts another execution when the queue resumes, rather than attaching to the existing work. findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts after an injected executor starts landing checks but before they finish. The queue starts a second execution and cannot recover the first execution's result.

findings.title: Executor events are never consumed
findings.detail: executeGate awaits only execution.result and never iterates execution.events. Local execution happens to report through a separate hooks closure, but an executor implementing the interface has no access to those hooks. Its check and status events are consequently absent from run events and landing logs, and an executor that relies on event consumption for progress can stall.

findings.failure_scenario: An injected executor emits a check event followed by a result. The gate verdict is recorded, but the run has no per-check event and the landing log has no check output.

findings.title: Local start does not start the execution
findings.detail: start only creates an ID and stores a signal; runLocalGates is invoked later by attach. This violates the requested executor contract that start starts work and attach reconnects to work already started. A caller using the interface directly can persist a valid handle and wait indefinitely for work that has never been launched.

findings.failure_scenario: A caller invokes start, persists the returned handle, and delays attachment while expecting the gate suite to run. No gate slot is acquired and no check starts until attach is called.

findings.title: Resolve the account home independently of HOME
findings.detail: os.homedir() uses the process HOME environment variable. If the daemon starts with HOME pointing to a different existing directory, the policy denies that directory and constructs editor credential paths beneath it, leaving the account's actual home readable by absolute path. SSH can still find its default keys through the account database, which is the distinction the request calls out.
findings.suggestion: Resolve and validate the account home independently of HOME, and cover a daemon environment whose HOME differs from the account home.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon starts with HOME set to a scratch or service directory while the account's SSH keys remain in its password-database home; a gate or editor reads those keys by their absolute path.

findings.title: Retry executions cannot be reattached after a restart

The new restart test explicitly expects that behavior, but the request requires restart attachment without starting the execution again.

findings.title: The handle is cleared before the result has a durable checkpoint

A restart after this save but before the caller's checkpoint loses both the execution identity and its result, so resume starts another execution. This also applies to successful initial executions, despite their reattachment support.
findings.suggestion: Keep the handle until the result and the stage's progress are durably saved together, or persist the result before clearing it.
findings.failure_scenario: A daemon restart occurs after the gate-result save and before the gates stage records lastGates. Resume sees no handle and starts the gate suite again.

findings.title: Landing checks do not persist their execution handle

findings.title: The handle is cleared before its result is checkpointed
findings.detail: A successful execution clears and saves the handle before returning its result to the stage. The caller has not yet saved the result or completed the stage. A restart in that interval loses both the execution identity and its result, so the resumed stage starts the suite again.

findings.title: Landing checks never persist their execution handle
findings.detail: The landing queue calls `executeGate` without a persistence callback or stored handle. Its handle therefore exists only in memory, and a restart cannot reattach to landing work even though landing checks are required to use the durable executor path.
findings.suggestion: Checkpoint the landing execution identity in durable queue state and supply it when the check resumes.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts during landing checks using an executor whose work survives the daemon. The queue starts a second suite instead of attaching to the first.

findings.title: Local start does not start an execution
findings.detail: `start` only records the request in memory; the gate work begins in `attach`. This breaks the requested executor contract that `start` starts work and `attach` reattaches to work already started. It also means a consumer that starts work and later attaches cannot rely on the returned handle representing running work.

findings.title: A cancelled land can be changed back to landed
findings.detail: The new post-merge lookup introduces an await between the merge result and the unconditional landed update. If cancellation or shutdown aborts that lookup, the catch converts the abort to null and landed() still runs, overwriting a cancelled queue entry and emitting a landed event.
findings.suggestion: After the lookup, recheck the abort signal and the current queue state before changing the entry; preserve a cancellation that won while the lookup was in flight.
findings.failure_scenario: A user cancels an entry while its post-merge GitHub lookup is pending. The lookup rejects on abort, then the queue changes the entry from cancelled to landed.

findings.title: Missing merge metadata can remain missing permanently
findings.detail: If the queue's single post-merge lookup fails or returns an observation that has not reached MERGED yet, it records null metadata. Reconciliation subsequently skips fetching every already-merged run and can only use a saved snapshot. With polling disabled or the PR untracked, no such snapshot need ever arrive, so the requested merge fields remain null.
findings.suggestion: Provide a bounded, retryable way to obtain a confirmed merge observation when the initial lookup lacks metadata, including when the poller does not track the PR.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub is temporarily unavailable immediately after a successful queue merge and polling is disabled. The run is marked merged with null fields and subsequent reconciliation passes never fetch its metadata.

findings.title: Backfilled metadata does not repair the merge feed item
findings.detail: The feed's run.merged trigger fires only when merged changes from false to true. When the initial queue observation lacks metadata, the feed item is created with null fields; this later update changes only the run fields, leaving the original feed item permanently inaccurate even if a later observation supplies both values.
findings.suggestion: Make the feed representation reflect the later confirmed metadata, or defer creating the merge item until its metadata is available while retaining reliable merge recording.
findings.failure_scenario: The first lookup returns no mergedBy or mergedAt, and a later poll supplies both. The run fields become populated but its run.merged feed item still reports null for both.

findings.title: MCP approvals still default to human

Existing clients and agents using the previously documented arguments therefore continue producing the exact misleading provenance the request asks to correct.
findings.suggestion: Require or otherwise obtain a consumer identity for MCP approvals, and ensure an MCP approval cannot silently fall back to human.
findings.failure_scenario: An existing MCP client calls limitless_review with run, verdict and reviewedSha but no consumer. Its review.approved item still has reviewer set to human.

findings.title: A cancelled land can be changed back to landed

findings.title: Merge metadata can remain missing permanently after a restart or failed lookup
findings.detail: The queue marks both runs merged before requesting metadata. If the daemon restarts during that request, or the request fails or times out, reconciliation only consults an existing saved snapshot and never fetches metadata for the merged run. The poller also excludes merged runs, so a pre-merge snapshot cannot be refreshed. The parent and round can therefore retain null merge fields indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: Make missing merge metadata durable pending work that reconciliation can fetch after a restart or transient failure.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub accepts a merge, the queue records it, and the daemon restarts before the metadata request completes while the saved PR snapshot still says OPEN.

findings.title: Landing feed events are not published after the outer transaction commits
findings.detail: The new outer database transaction encloses both landFeed and the run updates. Their publishFeed calls return while db.inTransaction is true, and no publication is triggered after this transaction commits. Subscribers and long-polling feed consumers can miss the landing and merge notifications until an unrelated later publication happens.
findings.suggestion: Use a Store transaction helper that queues publications and flushes them after the outermost commit.
findings.failure_scenario: A consumer is waiting on the feed when a PR lands and no later event occurs; the committed land.landed and run.merged items do not wake it.

findings.title: Enriching an already delivered feed item does not notify consumers
findings.detail: Metadata enrichment updates the existing feed row in place. A consumer that read and acknowledged the initial run.merged item with null fields will never receive the updated row because its feed cursor has already passed that item. Publishing the run update does not make the changed feed item readable again.
findings.suggestion: Provide a durable follow-up feed notification for metadata enrichment, or arrange for the original feed item to be emitted with the confirmed metadata.
findings.failure_scenario: A feed consumer reads the initial merge event while the queue's metadata request is in flight, then acknowledges it before the actor and timestamp are written.

findings.title: Consumer-named reviews fail against the previous daemon
findings.detail: The MCP proxy forwards the newly added consumer property to the daemon's review endpoint. The previous release validates review payloads with a strict schema that does not contain consumer, so an updated MCP client talking to an older running daemon receives a validation failure instead of recording the review.
findings.suggestion: Preserve compatibility with older daemons, for example by translating the consumer into the existing reviewer field before forwarding the request.
findings.failure_scenario: A newer MCP proxy submits limitless_review with consumer set while the daemon is still running the previous release.

output.summary: Reviewed all changed source paths and their surrounding call paths. The targeted test command produced 62 passes; four test files could not run because the MCP SDK modules were unavailable in the checkout.

findings.title: Interrupted metadata lookup can leave merge fields empty permanently
findings.detail: The queue marks the run merged before its metadata lookup, but reconciliation never fetches metadata for an already merged run. With polling disabled, or without a later saved merged snapshot, a failed lookup or daemon restart during that window leaves both fields null indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: Persist retryable metadata work or allow bounded reconciliation lookups for merged runs whose metadata is missing.
findings.failure_scenario: A queue merge succeeds, the daemon restarts before mergeMetadata completes, and the GitHub poller is disabled. Subsequent notifier passes skip fetching the merged PR, so the parent run and feed retain null mergedBy and mergedAt.

findings.title: Landing no longer records merges for failed or cancelled runs
findings.detail: The queue accepts runs with a PR regardless of status, but resolveMergedRun only updates succeeded, resolved, or needs_human runs. The previous landed implementation set merged on the target unconditionally. A successful land of a failed or cancelled run now produces a landed queue entry while leaving its run unmerged.
findings.suggestion: Record the confirmed merge for every status the queue accepts while preserving the existing status and resolution.
findings.failure_scenario: A run creates a PR and is then cancelled; a user approves and lands that PR through the queue. The entry becomes landed, but the run remains merged=false and receives no run.merged event.

findings.title: Consumer approvals fail against the previous daemon
findings.detail: The new MCP proxy forwards consumer in the review request. The previous daemon's strict ReviewVerdictSchema does not accept that field, so a newer CLI connected to an older daemon rejects the review instead of recording it.
findings.suggestion: Make the wire change compatible with the previous daemon, for example by encoding the prefixed identity in the existing reviewer field.
findings.failure_scenario: After updating the CLI but before restarting the daemon, an MCP client calls limitless_review with consumer set; the older daemon returns an invalid-review error.

findings.title: The reported change-view request still cannot identify the requested failure
findings.detail: The request specifically calls out a change-view request with run and file=1 after the head moves. Schema validation rejects that request before inspecting the current head or file list, and the new handler reports only that pagination pins are required. It therefore does not provide the requested changed head or unknown index for that input.
findings.suggestion: Preserve the pinning boundary while providing the relevant current-head or file-index diagnostic for the cited request.
findings.failure_scenario: Call limitless_get_change with {"run":"…","file":1} after a conflict round moves the head. The response says further reads require headSha and baseSha, without identifying the new head or the file-index failure.

output.summary: Reviewed both changed files and traced credential handling through the change view and review pipeline. The targeted MCP test could not start because the checkout lacks the MCP SDK dependency. A direct redaction check confirmed that another diff output still exposes multiline credentials.

findings.title: Review diffs still expose multiline credentials
findings.detail:
The new patch-line redaction is confined to the MCP change view. Conflict-resolution review diffs still pass through redactGateOutput and redactPrivate, neither of which reconstructs the diff sides before matching a multiline credential; the resulting patch is sent in the review prompt. The request explicitly requires other diff outputs to receive the same treatment or be listed as follow-ups, and no follow-up was provided. A direct check returned both credential lines unchanged: `bun -e 'import {registerCredential} from "./src/util/proc.ts"; import {redactGateOutput} from "./src/gates/output.ts"; registerCredential("TEST_MULTILINE_EXAMPLE", "alpha-secret-123
beta-secret-456"); console.log(redactGateOutput("+alpha-secret-123
+beta-secret-456
"))'` printed `+alpha-secret-123` and `+beta-secret-456` on separate lines.
findings.suggestion: Reuse a side-aware diff redactor for review patches before they are stored or sent to a model, or explicitly document this output as the requested follow-up.
findings.failure_scenario: A conflict-resolution diff adds a file containing a registered two-line credential. Git prefixes both lines with `+`, so the existing literal redactors do not match the credential, and both lines appear in the review prompt.

output.summary: Reviewed both changed files and the surrounding diff-rendering paths. The targeted MCP test could not start because the checkout lacks the MCP SDK dependency. A separate probe confirmed that ordinary credential redaction leaves a line-prefixed multiline credential intact.

findings.title: Review prompts can still expose multiline credentials in diffs
findings.detail: The verify-change review passes the Git patch into the model prompt, and conflict-resolution reviews also include a first-parent patch. These paths do not use the new patch-line redaction. Literal credential redaction cannot match a credential interrupted by diff prefixes, so both halves can be sent to the reviewer model. The request explicitly calls for other diff-rendering outputs to receive the same treatment or be listed as follow-ups; no follow-up was supplied. A targeted probe, `bun -e 'import { redactCredentials, registerCredential } from "./src/util/proc.ts"; registerCredential("TEST_REVIEW_SECRET", "alpha-secret-example\nbeta-secret-example"); console.log(redactCredentials("+alpha-secret-example\n+beta-secret-example"))'`, printed `+alpha-secret-example` and `+beta-secret-example` unchanged on separate lines.
findings.suggestion: Apply a shared patch-aware credential filter before diff text enters review prompts, including the first-parent patch, or explicitly record these diff outputs as follow-ups as permitted by the request.
findings.failure_scenario: A verify-change run reviews an added file containing a registered two-line credential; the generated patch contains each line with a `+` prefix and both lines reach the model prompt.

output.summary: Reviewed the setup, prompt, validation, cache and reporting paths. Focused tests could not run because the checkout has an incompatible Zod installation and a missing MCP SDK module.

findings.title: Setup failures count as failed review outcomes
findings.detail: A failed setup throws into the common error handler, which records pass=false. The summary's scoredTrial function includes error trials with a non-null pass value, including preparation failures. Consequently, a dependency installation failure counts against the review system's pass rate and paired comparisons even though no reviewer was invoked.
findings.suggestion: Exclude preparation failures from review scoring and paired comparisons while retaining them as reported trial errors.
findings.failure_scenario: A base setup command fails for one case; the prepared system receives a failed scored trial while the control system reviews the case, skewing the comparison.

findings.title: An exception during review overwrites preparation time
findings.detail: Review trials do not populate roundsUsed, so an exception after preparation reaches this branch and replaces preparationMs with the elapsed time since preparation began. That value includes the reviewer invocation and any later work, contrary to the requested separate preparation timing.
findings.suggestion: Track whether preparation has completed and only calculate failure preparation time for exceptions before that point.
findings.failure_scenario: Setup succeeds, then the reviewer invocation throws after several minutes; the reported preparation time includes those minutes.

output.summary: Reviewed the changed eval, prompt, schema and reporting paths. Targeted tests could not run because the checkout's installed dependencies lack the required Zod API and MCP SDK.

findings.title: Setup variants can be combined as duplicate routing evidence
findings.detail: Allowing setup to distinguish otherwise identical systems invalidates the policy selector's assumption that at most one standard single system exists per target. It accepts both systems and combines their trials under the same model, inflating the evidence and potentially changing routing-policy decisions.
findings.suggestion: Make policy selection distinguish or explicitly choose between setup variants, and test a run containing both variants for one target.
findings.failure_scenario: An eval contains standard single systems for the same model with setup omitted and setup true. Both pass validation, and selectEvidence counts both sets of trials as evidence for that model.

findings.title: Panel replay permits finders from a different setup condition
findings.detail: Setup is allowed on replay systems, but replay validation compares finder prompts, lenses and targets without comparing setup. A replay labeled setup true can therefore reuse finder results produced without dependencies, and the reverse is also accepted. Running setup in the replay worktree cannot change the already recorded finder results.
findings.suggestion: Require the replay source and destination to have matching setup settings, or explicitly represent differing finder and verifier preparation conditions.
findings.failure_scenario: A panel eval without setup is replayed by a system with setup true. Its finder calls are reconstructed from the unprepared source while the resulting trial is recorded as a prepared system.

findings.title: Invocation errors overwrite the recorded preparation time
findings.detail: Review trials do not set roundsUsed, so an exception after the reviewer starts satisfies this condition and replaces the completed preparation measurement with all elapsed time since preparation began. It also labels the error as a preparation failure, obscuring where the failure occurred.
findings.suggestion: Track whether preparation completed or invocation started separately, and preserve the completed preparationMs on later errors.
findings.failure_scenario: The harness throws after a review invocation has run for several minutes. The recorded preparationMs includes those minutes and preparationFailed is true.

output.summary: Reviewed the changed files and surrounding diff-redaction paths. The targeted MCP test could not start because @modelcontextprotocol/sdk is missing from the checkout.

findings.title: A credential match hides the entire file patch
findings.detail: When either blob contains a multiline credential, the change view returns a single withholding marker instead of mapping the match to its patch lines. This removes all unrelated changes and context from the file, including changes far from the credential. The new tests explicitly expect this behavior, although the acceptance criterion requires the rest of the file to stay visible.
findings.suggestion: Map matches in each reconstructed file side back to the affected patch lines, withhold those lines before paging, and retain unrelated lines.
findings.failure_scenario: An added file contains public lines before and after a two-line registered credential. Every page contains only the file-level withholding marker, so neither public line is available for review.

findings.title: Other rendered diffs still persist and transmit multiline credentials
findings.detail: The fix applies only to the MCP change view. The pipeline also stores diff.patch and includes patch text in review prompts; its literal credential redaction cannot match a credential split by unified-diff line prefixes. The request explicitly covers other outputs that render diffs or requires them to be listed as follow-ups, and this path remains exposed.
findings.suggestion: Apply shared multiline-aware diff redaction at these output boundaries, or document the specific remaining diff outputs as follow-ups as requested.
findings.failure_scenario: A verify-change run adds a file containing a registered credential on two lines. The unified patch contains each line with a '+' prefix, so both halves survive literal redaction in the stored diff artifact and review prompt.

output.summary: Reviewed the patch, surrounding privacy filters, report rendering, and changed tests. The targeted MCP test could not start because the checkout lacks @modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/stdio.js.

findings.title: A credential match hides the entire file
findings.detail: When either file side contains a multiline credential, the change replaces the complete patch with a file-level notice. This removes unrelated lines and does not meet the explicit acceptance criterion that the rest of the file stay visible. The new test asserts this behavior rather than checking that public neighbors remain visible.
findings.suggestion: Map matches on reconstructed file sides back to the affected patch lines and withhold those lines while retaining the rest of the patch.
findings.failure_scenario: An added file contains public text before and after a registered two-line credential. The change view returns only '[withheld: private text; 1 file]' and neither public line is available.

findings.title: Line-prefixed credentials can still escape through report pages
findings.detail: Report pages still apply literal privacy matching to the rendered report. A diff or quotation in a report inserts prefixes between credential lines, so neither the complete report check nor the final response check recognizes the registered value. The request explicitly includes other outputs that render diffs or quotations, and no follow-up is listed.
findings.suggestion: Apply prefix-aware multiline credential filtering to report text before paging, or explicitly record the remaining output as a follow-up as requested.
findings.failure_scenario: A persisted report contains a quoted diff with '+alpha-secret' and '+beta-secret' on consecutive lines, and 'alpha-secret\nbeta-secret' is registered. The report page returns both credential lines.

output.summary: Reviewed the changed gate execution, JUnit parsing, configuration, retry and persistence paths. The focused retry-files tests passed. The feedback and executor tests could not load because the checkout has incompatible or missing installed dependencies (Zod and the MCP SDK). A Bun reporter probe also exposed an incomplete failure list.

findings.title: Security checks can be classified as flaky after a retry
findings.detail: The retry selection and final classification do not distinguish security checks from ordinary checks. A security check that fails initially and passes its full retry is classified as flaky and made nonblocking. This leaves the request's explicit requirement that a security check failure never become a pass unimplemented.
findings.suggestion: Represent security checks in trusted gate configuration and preserve their blocking failure regardless of retry outcome; add a test for that path.
findings.failure_scenario: A configured security scan passes on baseline, fails after the change, and passes on its full retry. The comparison becomes flaky with blocking=false.

findings.title: Bun's report can omit failures while still yielding a targeted file list
findings.detail: Bun's JUnit reporter can omit a file that fails during module loading while reporting an ordinary test failure in another file. The parser accepts the reported file as a complete failure list, so the targeted retry omits the load failure instead of falling back to a full retry. A probe with one failing test and one file that throws at module load produced XML containing only the first file. This also leaves the omitted failure out of retry diagnostics.
findings.suggestion: Detect when Bun's report cannot account for the full failed run and treat the file list as unknown, then run the full retry. Cover a module-load failure alongside a reported test failure.
findings.failure_scenario: test/a.test.ts has a failing assertion and test/b.test.ts throws while loading. Bun reports only a.test.ts; its targeted retry fails, so the full suite is never rerun and the b.test.ts failure is omitted.

output.summary: Reviewed the retry flow, configuration provenance, JUnit parsing, slot policy, and changed tests. The retry-file tests passed. The executor and feedback tests could not load because installed dependencies were missing or mismatched.

findings.title: Changed-file failures skip the targeted retry
findings.detail: The existing output-location filter excludes a regression before its structured failure files are considered. Consequently, a test failure whose output points to a changed file receives no targeted retry, even when its failing files are known. The request requires a targeted retry for checks with a structured failure list. A direct invocation of retryRegressions with output `test/a.test.ts:12: failed`, that path in `changed`, and a known failing file returned `{"calls":0,"verdict":"regressed"}`.
findings.suggestion: Apply the changed-file shortcut only when targeted retry information is unavailable, or otherwise ensure known-file failures receive the requested targeted retry.
findings.failure_scenario: A change modifies a test file, and the failing test reports a line in that file. The gate immediately reports a regression without confirming the known failing files.

findings.title: A security check can still become nonblocking after a retry
findings.detail: Retry classification treats every check alike: a successful full retry becomes nonblocking `flaky`, and the gate configuration has no security-check marker used to prevent that transition. This leaves the request's explicit requirement that a security check failure never become a pass unimplemented.
findings.suggestion: Provide a trusted way to identify security checks and preserve a blocking failure when any attempt of such a check fails, with coverage for both targeted and full retries.
findings.failure_scenario: A configured security check fails on its first post-change run and succeeds on its full retry; the result is classified as nonblocking flaky.

output.summary: Reviewed the listener, pairing, heartbeat, configuration, persistence and tests as the first half of the requested split. Targeted tests could not run because the checkout resolved a missing MCP SDK and an incompatible Zod version; neither error was treated as a finding.

findings.title: Pairing code does not authenticate the initial TLS connection
findings.detail: The first request accepts any TLS certificate, and the coordinator returns both the comparison code and claim secret over that connection. An active network intermediary can forward the real request and response, display the genuine code to the worker, then claim the approved token itself. Comparing the codes does not detect the intermediary, and the worker pins the intermediary's certificate.
findings.suggestion: Bind the owner-verified code to the actual TLS endpoints or otherwise authenticate the coordinator before disclosing the claim secret.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker intercepts a worker's initial pairing connection, proxies the request to the coordinator, and forwards its code. The owner sees matching codes and approves; the attacker uses the observed secret to obtain the worker token.

findings.title: Worker credentials are protected only in the worker process
findings.detail: Private-read registrations are process-local. The worker CLI registers its token and fingerprint in its own process, but a daemon on the same machine builds agent sandboxes from a different registry. The default credential deny list does not include these files under ~/.limitless/worker, so a tool-enabled editor can read the token. The same issue affects the coordinator TLS key whenever its listener is disabled after the key has been created.
findings.suggestion: Register these persistent credential paths in every daemon before agents can start, regardless of whether the worker or listener is currently running.
findings.failure_scenario: A machine runs both the worker CLI and a Limitless daemon. An editor launched by the daemon reads ~/.limitless/worker/token and can authenticate as the paired worker.

findings.title: Interrupted certificate generation leaves the listener permanently unable to start
findings.detail: The key file is created before openssl runs, but failures and interruptions leave it in place. A later start detects incomplete TLS material and throws rather than recovering, preventing the daemon from starting while the listener is configured.
findings.suggestion: Generate both files under temporary names and publish them together, or clean up incomplete first-generation material safely.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon is stopped or openssl fails after key.pem is created but before cert.pem is written. Every subsequent daemon start fails with 'Incomplete worker TLS material' until an owner manually repairs the directory.

findings.title: An approved but unclaimed pairing permanently reserves the worker name
findings.detail: Approval changes the row to approved immediately, while claiming is refused after the original ten-minute expiry. If the worker disconnects before claiming and returns after expiry, it has no token and cannot pair again under its existing name because approved rows are always rejected.
findings.suggestion: Permit recovery of expired, unclaimed approvals or make the approval and claim lifecycle distinguish an issued token from an unclaimed one.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner approves a request while the worker is offline for more than ten minutes. The worker's claim expires, and a new pairing with the same name fails until the owner manually revokes it.

output.summary: Reviewed the pairing and heartbeat split, including restart and sandbox boundaries. Targeted tests could not run: `bun test test/workers.test.ts test/config-routing.test.ts` encountered a missing `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` module and an incompatible installed Zod version. Assumed the documented first-PR split is intentional.

findings.title: Pairing code does not authenticate the coordinator connection
findings.detail: The first TLS connection accepts any certificate, and the worker pins the certificate observed on that connection. An active network attacker can proxy the initial pairing request to the real coordinator, relay its code to the worker, and relay the claim after the owner approves that same code. The attacker receives the issued token and the worker pins the attacker's certificate. Comparing the displayed codes does not detect this relay because the code is not bound to the TLS connection.
findings.suggestion: Bind the owner-verified pairing code to the coordinator certificate or use another authenticated pairing exchange that prevents relaying the claim.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker intercepts a worker's first connection while the owner compares and approves the genuine coordinator's displayed code.

findings.title: Worker credentials are protected only in the worker process
findings.detail: Private-file registrations are process-local. The worker CLI registers its token and fingerprint only in its own process, so a separately running factory daemon does not add them to its agent sandbox deny rules. Likewise, the coordinator TLS key is registered only while its listener is enabled; disabling the listener leaves the existing key unprotected in later daemon sessions. Tool-enabled agent sandboxes can read ordinary files under the home directory unless explicitly denied, so they can read these persisted credentials.
findings.suggestion: Register all persisted worker credential and TLS key paths in every daemon process before starting agents, independently of whether the worker listener or worker CLI is running.
findings.failure_scenario: A machine runs both a paired worker CLI and the factory daemon; an editor agent reads the worker token from the default worker data directory.

findings.title: Interrupted certificate creation leaves the listener unable to start
findings.detail: Certificate generation creates the final key path before invoking OpenSSL. If generation fails or the daemon stops before both files are complete, the partial material remains. The next start rejects an incomplete pair, or attempts to use invalid files, and the daemon cannot start with the worker listener enabled until an operator removes the partial files.
findings.suggestion: Generate and validate both files under temporary names, then publish them together, and clean up incomplete temporary material on failure.
findings.failure_scenario: OpenSSL fails or the daemon is interrupted during the first certificate generation; every subsequent listener startup fails on the leftover key or certificate.

output.summary: Reviewed the pairing, TLS, heartbeat, configuration, owner API, and persistence changes. The requested split permits gate jobs to follow in a later change. Targeted tests could not load because the checkout is missing @simplewebauthn/server and has an incompatible Zod installation.

findings.title: Heartbeat capabilities can persist a worker token in plaintext
findings.detail: The authenticated heartbeat is stored as raw JSON without credential redaction. Its string fields accept the 64-character bearer token, so an approved worker can cause its token to be stored in the database despite the requirement to store only its hash. Authentication registers the token for redaction, but that redaction is not applied before this write.
findings.suggestion: Redact credential-bearing capability data before persisting or exposing it, while retaining the validated values needed for version matching.
findings.failure_scenario: An approved worker sends its bearer token as osVersion in a valid heartbeat. The token is written verbatim to workers.capabilities.

findings.title: Interrupted certificate creation leaves listener unable to start
findings.detail: Certificate generation creates the key file before invoking OpenSSL, but the error path leaves partial files in place. A subsequent start treats either file without the other as incomplete material and refuses to start. With the worker listener configured, this also prevents the daemon from starting until the files are manually repaired.
findings.suggestion: Generate both files in temporary paths and publish them together, or clean up newly created partial material on failure.
findings.failure_scenario: OpenSSL fails or the daemon stops after key.pem is created but before cert.pem is written; every subsequent daemon start fails with 'Incomplete worker TLS material'.

output.summary: Reviewed the pairing, heartbeat, TLS, persistence, CLI and startup paths. The requested first split is implemented, but recovery from interrupted pairing and TLS failures needs work. The targeted command `bun test test/workers.test.ts test/api-token-http.test.ts test/config-routing.test.ts` could not run: this checkout could not resolve `@simplewebauthn/server`, and the resolved Zod version lacked `z.number().overwrite`. No test assertions ran.

findings.title: A transient claim failure strands an approved pairing
findings.detail: The claim request has no retry or persisted claim state. If it fails after the owner approves, the worker exits without storing its token, while the coordinator keeps the name in the approved state and rejects another pairing request for that name.
findings.suggestion: Retry transient claim failures until the pairing expires, or persist enough state to resume the claim after a restart.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner approves a pairing just as a network interruption causes the worker's next claim request to fail. Restarting the pairing command with the same name is refused until the owner manually revokes it.

findings.title: Certificate pin failures are retried silently forever
findings.detail: The heartbeat loop treats every transport exception as transient, including a coordinator fingerprint mismatch. A worker whose coordinator certificate changes remains running but never reports why it is offline, so the documented recovery of pairing again is not prompted.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish certificate pin failures and other permanent configuration errors from transient transport errors and report them to the operator.
findings.failure_scenario: The coordinator's TLS certificate is replaced and the worker reconnects with its old pinned fingerprint. Every heartbeat fails verification and is retried indefinitely without an actionable error.

findings.title: Interrupted certificate generation prevents subsequent starts
findings.detail: Certificate creation publishes the key path before OpenSSL completes, and the failure path leaves partial material in place. Later starts reject an incomplete pair, or attempt to parse invalid material if both paths exist, rather than recovering from the interrupted first attempt.
findings.suggestion: Generate both files under temporary names and publish them only after validating the completed pair, cleaning up partial files on failure.
findings.failure_scenario: OpenSSL fails or the daemon stops during first-start certificate generation. The next daemon start encounters the retained partial key or certificate and fails to start the configured worker listener.

findings.title: Pairing expiration assumes synchronized machine clocks
findings.detail: The coordinator sends an absolute expiration timestamp, but the worker compares it with its own wall clock. The protocol does not account for clock skew, so a valid coordinator-side request can expire immediately on the worker.
findings.suggestion: Use a duration measured by the worker's monotonic clock, while retaining coordinator-side expiration enforcement.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker's clock is more than ten minutes ahead of the coordinator. It prints the pairing code and immediately exits as expired even though the coordinator still considers the request pending.

output.summary: Reviewed the worker protocol, leasing, execution, validation, restart, and cache paths. The targeted command `bun test test/workers.test.ts test/gate-executor.test.ts test/config-routing.test.ts` could not execute tests: local dependencies lack `@simplewebauthn/server` and provide a Zod version without `z.number().overwrite`.

findings.title: Infrastructure retries can erase an already reported failing check
findings.detail: Check events are retained for display, but a failed lease is requeued without preserving its check outcomes in the eventual GateRun. If a worker posts a failing check and disconnects before posting its final result, another worker or the local fallback can return a pass, and that passing result becomes the gate outcome. This violates the requirement that infrastructure retries never turn a failing check into a pass.
findings.suggestion: Carry completed check failures into the final outcome across infrastructure attempts, or otherwise prevent a later passing attempt from overriding an observed failure.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker posts a failed test event, loses its connection before posting the final result, and the same flaky test passes on the next worker; the coordinator records a passing gate run.

findings.title: Cache the executor that actually produced the baseline
findings.detail: The baseline cache key is selected from configuration before execution. When both LAN attempts fail, the executor runs the baseline locally but stores it under the LAN key. A later run can reuse that local baseline while its post-change gates run on a worker with a different environment, producing incorrect regression comparisons.
findings.suggestion: Record the executor that produced the result and avoid caching a local fallback under the LAN environment key.
findings.failure_scenario: No worker is available during baseline preparation, so a local passing baseline is cached as LAN. A worker later becomes available and runs the change in an environment where the same unchanged check fails; the comparison reports a regression.

findings.title: Allow an in-flight LAN job to resume after switching back to local
findings.detail: A persisted LAN handle is rejected when the current configured executor is local. Switching the configuration back to local before rollback is explicitly documented, and daily daemon restarts can occur while a LAN job is in flight. On restart, the run encounters `Unavailable gate executor: lan` instead of reattaching or safely resolving the existing job.
findings.suggestion: Provide a durable resume path for LAN handles independently of the current selection for new jobs, including cancellation or completion of the existing job.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator changes `gates.executor` from `lan` to `local` while a run is waiting on a leased job, then restarts the daemon; the resumed stage fails on its stored LAN handle.

output.summary: Reviewed the worker lease, result validation, fallback, checkpoint, and configuration paths. Targeted tests could not run: the checkout's available dependencies lack the MCP SDK and expose a Zod version without number().overwrite().

findings.title: Restart discards in-flight retry jobs
findings.detail: Only baseline, initial, and rebase handles are reattached. A shutdown during a timeout or regression retry preserves its LAN handle, but resume cancels that job and starts another execution. A retry that already completed before the restart can therefore be repeated, and its recorded result is lost.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough retry state to reattach every durable LAN execution and consume its result after restart.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while a worker is running a regression retry or after the worker posts its result but before the pipeline saves it.

findings.title: A final result can contradict an already reported failing check
findings.detail: Check events and the final run are validated independently. The coordinator accepts a failing event followed by a passing final result for the same requested check, and the pipeline grades the final result as a pass. The worker protocol explicitly treats results as untrusted and requires failures never to become passes.
findings.suggestion: Reconcile the final run with the accepted events for the current lease, rejecting contradictory or missing evidence as an infrastructure failure.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker posts a valid failing check event, then posts a schema-valid passing GateRun with the requested SHA and check names.

findings.title: Worker reports the SHA measured before running gates
findings.detail: The worker reads HEAD before executing setup and checks, then posts that saved value without verifying the checkout afterward. Gate commands can modify the checkout, including replacing its writable .git file. The coordinator's later HEAD check examines its own unchanged checkout, so it cannot detect a worker checkout that no longer represents the requested commit.
findings.suggestion: Revalidate the worker checkout and trusted Git administration after gates finish, and report an infrastructure failure if HEAD or its trusted paths changed.
findings.failure_scenario: A gate modifies the worker checkout's Git metadata or changes the checkout during execution and exits successfully; the result is still attested to the original SHA.

findings.title: Changing back to local leaves active LAN runs unable to resume
findings.detail: A persisted LAN handle requires the currently configured executor to have kind lan. If the operator resets the configuration to local, including as directed before rolling back, a run interrupted at its gate checkpoint fails with an unavailable-executor error instead of resuming or safely cancelling and rerunning the work. The previous release also cannot attach this newly introduced handle.
findings.suggestion: Provide a durable migration or recovery path for pending LAN handles when LAN execution is disabled or the release is rolled back.
findings.failure_scenario: A deploy restarts the daemon during a LAN gate, then the operator resets gates.executor to local for rollback or to disable workers.

output.summary: Reviewed all four changed files and the retry, confinement, logging, and restart paths. The targeted gate retry tests passed. The land queue tests could not load because the installed dependencies lack @modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js.

findings.title: A confinement failure in one check does not prevent other retries
findings.detail: The queue selects and runs targeted retries before inspecting the complete gate run for confinement failures. If one check reports a confinement failure and another reports failed files, the latter is retried even though the request explicitly requires a confinement failure to block with no retry. The eventual result still blocks, but the additional command can wait for a slot or run for its full timeout before the queue reports the confinement failure.
findings.suggestion: Inspect setup and all check results for confinement failures before starting any targeted retry, and block immediately when one is present.
findings.failure_scenario: A test check fails with failedFiles while a separate lint check reports a confinement failure. The test retry runs before the land is blocked.

findings.title: Restart can erase the log supporting a recorded flaky landing
findings.detail: The flaky reason and warning event are persisted before the checked head is checkpointed as waiting for CI. If the daemon restarts after that write but before the checkpoint, the checking phase runs again and truncates the same land log. A clean second run leaves the old flaky reason in place, but the first failure and successful targeted retry that justify it are no longer in the log.
findings.suggestion: Preserve the prior attempt's log across a checking restart, or durably associate the flaky outcome and its evidence with the checked head before recording it as the landing outcome.
findings.failure_scenario: A targeted retry passes, the flaky reason is stored, and the daemon restarts during the subsequent private-range check or push. On resume the full checks pass, the entry lands as flaky, and its log contains neither the original failure nor the retry.

output.summary: Reviewed the retry, logging, and restart paths. The targeted gate retry tests passed, but the land queue tests could not load because the MCP SDK dependency is missing in the environment.

findings.title: A restart can erase the evidence for a recorded flaky landing
findings.detail: The flaky reason is persisted before the land is checkpointed as waiting for CI. If the daemon restarts in that window, the entry resumes from checking and checks() truncates the same land log. A subsequent clean check leaves the old flaky reason in place, so the entry can land marked flaky even though its log no longer contains the first failure or retry. This violates the requirement to retain both attempts in the land log.
findings.suggestion: Make the flaky record and its log durable across a checking restart, or clear stale flake state when restarting checks and preserve the prior attempt's log separately.
findings.failure_scenario: A targeted retry passes, the flaky reason is stored, and the daemon restarts before pushedSha is checkpointed. On resume the full check passes; the entry lands with the old flaky reason but its log contains only the resumed clean run.

output.summary: Reviewed all changed files and traced verifier execution, smoke evidence, and lease fallback. Targeted tests could not load because the checkout's available dependencies lack the sandbox runtime and MCP SDK, and its resolved Zod version lacks prefault.

findings.title: Allow the Bun executable that verifier commands resolve
findings.detail: The allowance covers only the daemon's process.execPath. A verifier runs `bun test` through its shell PATH, which can resolve to a different installation under a denied private root. That executable remains denied, so the reported hang can persist. The new smoke check also invokes process.execPath explicitly, so it can pass while the verifier's actual `bun test` fails.
findings.suggestion: Resolve the Bun executable from the verifier's effective command environment, grant its validated path, and have the smoke check exercise that same resolution.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon starts with Bun from one installation, while the verifier shell's PATH selects another Bun under the user's home directory.

findings.title: Do not treat sandbox-denied connections as an unavailable coordinator
findings.detail: Classifying EPERM as a preconnection failure makes a wrapped test run without a lease when the sandbox denies both transports, even if the coordinator is healthy and its gate lane is occupied. This bypasses the configured concurrency limit and the test duration cap for ordinary Claude reader commands.
findings.suggestion: Keep sandbox-denied coordination fail-closed, or provide a transport that the reader can use to obtain the lease.
findings.failure_scenario: A Claude reader runs a wrapped full `bun test` while another full suite holds the gate lane; both connection attempts return EPERM and the new fallback starts the second suite immediately.

output.summary: Reviewed the changed harness, lease and smoke-check paths. Targeted tests could not run because the checkout lacks required dependencies and resolves an incompatible Zod version.

findings.title: Smoke probe bypasses the Bun executable verifiers invoke
findings.detail: The probe executes the daemon's absolute process.execPath, and the new read allowance grants that same executable. A verifier normally invokes `bun test` through its shell PATH, which can resolve to a different Bun installation. In that case the smoke check passes while the verifier's Bun remains denied by read confinement, leaving the reported verification failure unresolved.
