The regression test also uses process.execPath in verifier mode, so it does not catch this mismatch.
findings.suggestion: Resolve and permit the Bun executable available to the verifier's shell, and have the live probe execute `bun test` through that same environment.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon starts with one Bun executable, while the verifier's PATH resolves `bun` to another installation under a denied private root. The smoke check passes using the daemon executable, but the verifier cannot run `bun test`.

output.summary: Reviewed the publication rewrite and its PR, round-comment, and squash-body call sites. The targeted publication test could not start because the checkout lacks the entities package. Direct execution of the rewrite function confirmed that some local paths remain in published Markdown.

findings.title: Local paths in link labels and file URLs remain publishable
findings.detail: The link alternative consumes an entire Markdown link, but the callback examines only its destination. A local path in the label is therefore never rewritten when the destination is relative. A file:// destination also fails the root comparison and is returned unchanged. Either form can disclose the owner's username and data layout in a public PR; once that username is added to private-strings, it can instead block delivery. A direct execution check returned `[/factory/data/work/run/test/a.ts](test/a.ts) => [/factory/data/work/run/test/a.ts](test/a.ts)` and `[file](file:///factory/data/work/run/test/a.ts) => [file](file:///factory/data/work/run/test/a.ts)`.
findings.suggestion: Sanitize local paths in link labels as well as destinations, and recognize local file URLs before comparing them with the configured roots. Add publication tests for both forms.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer report contains `[/Users/owner/.limitless/work/run/test/a.ts](test/a.ts)` or `[file](file:///Users/owner/.limitless/work/run/test/a.ts)`.

findings.title: The data placeholder is interpreted as an HTML tag in Markdown
findings.detail: The replacement emits `<data>` literally into Markdown. GitHub interprets that as an HTML opening tag, so the requested plain-text placeholder is not displayed as written. For example, a log link is rewritten to `<data>/runs/log.txt`, whose visible text omits the placeholder and leaves a misleading absolute-looking path.
findings.suggestion: Escape the placeholder for Markdown or otherwise render it as visible plain text, while preserving the intended displayed value.
findings.failure_scenario: A report links to a log under the factory data directory and the resulting PR body or comment is rendered on GitHub.

output.summary: Reviewed all changed files and traced the PR body, round-comment, and squash-body paths. A targeted probe confirmed publication bypasses; the normal test files could not run because the checkout lacks the entities dependency.

findings.title: Local paths in link labels and file URLs pass through unchanged
findings.detail: The link regex consumes the entire Markdown link, but the replacement checks only its destination. A local path in the label is therefore never examined when the destination is relative. A file:// destination also fails the root comparison. Either form can publish the owner's username and data layout; once that username is listed as private, delivery instead fails its privacy check. A targeted probe returned the original strings unchanged. Command: bun -e 'const s=await Bun.file("src/gates/publication.ts").text(); const code=s.slice(s.indexOf("export function sanitizePublication"),s.indexOf("/** Check both" )).replace("export function", "function"); const f=Function(new Bun.Transpiler({loader:"ts"}).transformSync(code)+";return sanitizePublication")(); const w="/Users/alice/.limitless/work/run", d="/Users/alice/.limitless"; for (const x of [`[${w}/a.ts](a.ts)`,`[file](${w.replace("alice","alice")}/a.ts)`,`[file](file://${w}/a.ts)`,`![diagram](${w}/diagram.png)`]) console.log(JSON.stringify([x,f(x,w,d)]));'. Relevant output: ["[/Users/alice/.limitless/work/run/a.ts](a.ts)","[/Users/alice/.limitless/work/run/a.ts](a.ts)"] and ["[file](file:///Users/alice/.limitless/work/run/a.ts)","[file](file:///Users/alice/.limitless/work/run/a.ts)"].
findings.suggestion: Sanitize path-bearing link labels as well as destinations, and recognize local file URLs before comparing their paths with the configured roots.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer reports `[/Users/alice/.limitless/work/run/a.ts](a.ts)` or `[file](file:///Users/alice/.limitless/work/run/a.ts)`.

findings.title: Encoded local paths bypass rewriting
findings.detail: Root comparisons operate on the literal Markdown destination, although GitHub interprets character references in it. The targeted probe in the preceding finding returned `[file](/Users/alice/.limitless/work/run/a.ts)` unchanged. Thus an encoded username can be exposed in the published link; if the decoded username is in private-strings, the existing decoded-text check blocks delivery instead.
findings.suggestion: Decode Markdown destination character references before matching local roots, then serialize the sanitized result safely.
findings.failure_scenario: A report links to `/Users/alice/.limitless/work/run/a.ts`, which resolves to a path under the run's worktree.

findings.title: Image links become ordinary links
findings.detail: The matcher accepts image syntax but always emits a normal link, removing the `!`. The targeted probe in the first finding returned `[diagram.png](diagram.png)` for `![diagram](/Users/alice/.limitless/work/run/diagram.png)`, so a report image no longer renders.
findings.suggestion: Preserve the image marker when rewriting a worktree image destination.
findings.failure_scenario: A report embeds an image using an absolute worktree path.

output.summary: Reviewed the changed land queue, store, and tests against the claim-loss requirements. The targeted command `bun test test/land-queue.test.ts` could not start because `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js` is missing from the checkout. The review found remaining claim-loss races in the push, merge, and worktree paths.

findings.title: Ownership can change inside the merge and push helpers before they issue commands
findings.detail: The ownership checks run before calling helpers that themselves await multiple operations. `mergePullRequest` awaits a GitHub PR lookup before issuing `gh pr merge`, and `pushExistingBranch` awaits Git and remote lookups before issuing its push. A reclaim during one of those awaits leaves the old worker's signal live until its next heartbeat, so it can still issue the command after losing its claim. This misses the request's explicit requirement that a worker which lost its claim issue no merge or push.
findings.suggestion: Pass an ownership guard into these helpers and check it immediately before each merge or push command, including retries.
findings.failure_scenario: The old worker enters `mergePullRequest`, its PR view is delayed, another owner reclaims the stale entry, and the view returns before the next heartbeat; the old worker then runs `gh pr merge`.

findings.title: A displaced worker can remove the new owner's worktree
findings.detail: The old worker always calls `discard` in its `finally` block, even when an ownership check throws after a reclaim. Both attempts use the same `land-<entry id>` path. If the new owner has already recreated that checkout, the old worker removes its Git worktree and directory, causing the new attempt's commands to fail or its work to be lost.
findings.suggestion: Give attempts isolated worktree paths or otherwise coordinate cleanup so a displaced worker cannot remove a newer owner's checkout.
findings.failure_scenario: The old worker is waiting on CI, another process reclaims the entry and creates its checkout, then the old CI response arrives; the old worker detects claim loss and its `finally` removes the new checkout.

findings.title: Reclaim before the push leaves a checkpoint for a commit that was never published
findings.detail: The worker records `pushedSha` before the asynchronous push. If ownership changes before the push occurs, the new owner resumes as though that commit was published. It checks out the recorded SHA and waits for CI on it, although the remote branch still points to the approved SHA; depending on object availability, recovery either fails checkout or waits until CI times out. Preventing the displaced push therefore also requires reconciling this checkpoint on resume.
findings.suggestion: On recovery, distinguish a recorded push intent from a confirmed remote push and safely resume or retry when the remote still has the approved head.
findings.failure_scenario: A base merge creates a new head, the old worker records it in `pushedSha`, and the entry is reclaimed before the actual push. The replacement worker resumes with that SHA while GitHub never received it.

output.summary: Reviewed the changed claim checks and surrounding land and CI paths. The targeted command `bun test test/land-queue.test.ts` could not start because `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js` is missing. Two paths still allow a worker that lost its claim to write or disrupt the replacement worker.

findings.title: CI inspection can persist results after the claim is reclaimed
findings.detail: Passing `current` to `ciDecision` does not guard every write after an awaited GitHub response. In `inspectCi`, the default-branch check responses are followed by feed and setting writes before the next `current()` check; a rerun response similarly updates the failure record without rechecking ownership. The old worker can therefore write after a reclaim, despite the requested guarantee.
findings.suggestion: Make the claim check and each land-initiated CI outcome write atomic, including writes following default-branch inspection and rerun responses.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker awaits the default-branch CI checks or a rerun response, another owner reclaims the entry, and the response arrives before the old worker's heartbeat. The old inspection writes CI settings, feed items, or a rerun outcome.

findings.title: A displaced worker can remove the replacement worker's checkout
findings.detail: The `finally` block always discards the entry's fixed worktree path, even when an ownership check throws after a reclaim. The replacement worker uses that same path, so the old worker's asynchronous cleanup can remove its checkout while it is checking or preparing a merge. The checkout setup also removes that shared path without a claim check after its preceding await.
findings.suggestion: Isolate worktree paths by claim attempt or otherwise coordinate checkout creation and cleanup so an old attempt cannot remove a newer attempt's files.
findings.failure_scenario: Worker A waits for CI, worker B reclaims and starts using `land-<entry id>`, then A's CI response arrives. A detects the lost claim and enters `finally`, deleting B's worktree and causing B's land attempt to fail.

output.summary: Reviewed the claim checks, CI inspection, Git operations, and changed tests. Targeted tests could not start because checkout dependencies are missing: the land queue test could not resolve @modelcontextprotocol/sdk, and the CI classifier and GitHub delivery tests could not resolve entities.

findings.title: A refused push leaves a checkpoint that prevents the replacement from pushing
findings.detail: The worker records pushedSha before pushExistingBranch performs its internal asynchronous checks. If the entry is reclaimed during those checks, the new guard correctly refuses the push, but the replacement inherits pushedSha and treats the commit as already pushed. It waits for CI on a commit that is still only local, eventually blocking the land instead of completing it. The new push-guard test verifies that the remote remains unchanged but does not resume the replacement worker.
findings.suggestion: On resume, reconcile the recorded SHA with the remote head and safely push it when the remote still has the approved SHA, while preserving recovery when the earlier push actually succeeded.
findings.failure_scenario: A base merge is required; the old worker records its merge commit, loses its claim during pushExistingBranch's remote lookup, and the guard aborts before git push. The new owner resumes with pushedSha set while the PR still points to approvedSha.

output.summary: Reviewed the changed claim guards, retry paths, CI classification, cleanup, and tests. Targeted tests could not load because the checkout lacks the @modelcontextprotocol/sdk and entities dependencies.

findings.title: A refused push leaves a checkpoint for a commit that was never pushed
findings.detail: The worker records pushedSha before pushExistingBranch performs its asynchronous preparation and ownership guard. If another worker reclaims the entry during that preparation, the guard prevents the push, but the new owner resumes from pushedSha as though the commit were already on GitHub. It then waits for CI on a commit that was never published and eventually blocks the entry.
findings.suggestion: Make the pre-push checkpoint distinguish an intended push from a confirmed push, and reconcile the remote head on resume before waiting for CI.
findings.failure_scenario: A base merge produces a new SHA; the old worker records it, loses its claim while pushExistingBranch awaits ls-remote, and the guard refuses the push. The new owner finds the approved SHA still on the PR and waits for CI on the unpublished SHA.

findings.title: Claim loss can strand a rejected CI rerun as pending
findings.detail: The rerun is durably marked rerun_requested before the API call. If ownership changes while that call is in flight, the new guard discards its response. When GitHub rejected the request, no later attempt exists to resolve the pending record, and subsequent inspections continue waiting for a newer attempt rather than recording the rejection.
findings.suggestion: Provide a durable reconciliation path for an unconfirmed rerun request, including a rejected response after claim loss.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub returns a 4xx rejection to a rerun request after the land entry has been reclaimed. The old worker discards the response; the new worker repeatedly sees rerun_requested with the original workflow attempt and eventually times out CI.

findings.title: A displaced worker can still write into the new attempt's gate log
findings.detail: Gate result callbacks append to a shared per-entry log without checking ownership. A reclaimed worker can report a result before its next heartbeat while the new attempt has already truncated and started writing the same log, mixing old results into the new attempt's persisted evidence. This also leaves the request's requirement that a worker which lost its claim writes nothing unmet.
findings.suggestion: Guard gate-log writes against claim loss and use attempt-specific log paths so overlapping attempts cannot alter each other's evidence.
findings.failure_scenario: A gate remains in flight when its claim is reclaimed. The new worker starts checks and writes land-<id>.log; the old gate then completes and appends its result to that same file.

output.summary: Reviewed the land queue, persistence, CI handling, and changed tests. The focused store tests passed. The queue tests could not run because the checkout is missing @modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js.

findings.title: Rollback blocks active unowned lands
findings.detail: Unowned entries are persisted with an empty run_id. The previous release reads that value as a run ID and its land queue fails with “run  is gone” when it resumes the entry. A rollback during a queued or in-progress land therefore permanently blocks that land instead of allowing the previous release to continue processing it.
findings.suggestion: Provide a rollback-compatible representation and processing path for active unowned entries, or explicitly prevent the old release from claiming them while preserving a path for the new release to resume them.
findings.failure_scenario: An unowned PR is waiting for CI when deployment rolls back to the previous release; the old daemon claims the entry and marks it blocked because no run has ID "".

findings.title: Unowned PR numbers are rejected
findings.detail: The existing land command accepts a PR number or #number, but the new unowned path accepts only a full GitHub URL. Consequently, the requested `limitless land <pr> --sha <full sha>` workflow fails for an unowned PR specified in the same number form supported for factory PRs.
findings.suggestion: Resolve a PR number against the configured repository context, with a clear ambiguity error when multiple repositories could match.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator runs `limitless land 599 --sha <full-sha>` for a hand-opened PR; the command returns “run not found” instead of queuing it.

findings.title: Rejecting every fork PR excludes requested open PRs
findings.detail: The request covers open PRs on configured GitHub repositories and does not exclude PRs whose head is in a fork. This unconditional rejection prevents those PRs from entering the land queue, including cases where the base is already an ancestor and no head-branch push is necessary.
findings.suggestion: Support fork PRs through the same pinned checks and merge flow, handling any required base update according to the actual head repository and its permissions.
findings.failure_scenario: A contributor opens an up-to-date PR from a fork against a configured repository and supplies its full head SHA; the request fails with “cross-repository pull requests cannot be landed”.

output.summary: Reviewed the changed queue, persistence, CI classification, and tests. The seven land-store tests passed. The land-queue test file could not load because the checkout lacks @modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js, so its behavior was checked by tracing the code.

findings.title: Accept PR numbers for unowned lands
findings.detail: The new path accepts only a full GitHub URL, although the requested command is `limitless land <pr> --sha <full sha>` and the existing CLI accepts PR numbers. A bare number with no matching factory run returns `run not found`; if another configured repository has a factory run with the same PR number, the initial lookup can instead select that unrelated run.
findings.suggestion: Resolve the requested PR number against an unambiguous configured repository, and refuse clearly when repository selection is ambiguous.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator runs `limitless land 599 --sha <current-full-sha>` for a hand-opened PR. It is rejected even though the PR is open on a configured repository.

findings.title: Support open PRs whose head is in a fork
findings.detail: The implementation rejects every cross-repository PR. The request covers open PRs on configured GitHub repositories without excluding fork contributions, so these PRs cannot receive the requested confined land checks.
findings.suggestion: Support fetching and updating the actual head repository with the same SHA lease and publication checks, or provide a way to perform the checked merge without pushing to the fork.
findings.failure_scenario: A person opens a PR from their fork against a configured repository and supplies its exact current SHA; the request fails with `cross-repository pull requests cannot be landed`.

findings.title: Preserve active unowned lands across rollback
findings.detail: An unowned entry is persisted with an empty run ID. If a deploy rolls back while that entry is active, the previous release resumes it, looks up the empty run ID, and marks it blocked as `run  is gone`. This loses the in-progress land and can happen during the normal daily restart or rollback window.
findings.suggestion: Use a representation and rollout strategy that the previous release can safely resume or leave pending without blocking the entry.
findings.failure_scenario: A new release queues an unowned land and is rolled back while it is checking or waiting for CI. The old daemon claims the row and permanently blocks it because no run with ID `""` exists.

output.summary: Reviewed cleanup persistence, recovery, startup, resume paths, and the changed tests. The targeted cleanup test command passed eight tests; three integration tests could not run because @modelcontextprotocol/sdk was unavailable in the environment.

findings.title: Recovery clears the record without discovering descendants missed by the interrupted sweep
findings.detail: Recovery kills only the PIDs already recorded. The live sweep deliberately rescans after freezing because a marked process can fork after the initial snapshot. If the daemon dies before that rescan records the new descendant, recovery deletes the invocation's records and permits the next command while that descendant remains alive and can write to the checkout. A crash during the initial scan before the first record has the same absence of durable recovery intent.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough invocation identity and cleanup intent before discovery to resume the marked-process sweep, and clear it only after the complete set has been found and terminated.
findings.failure_scenario: A marked parent forks after the first process snapshot but before SIGSTOP; the daemon dies immediately after freezing the parent. On restart, recovery kills the recorded parent, deletes the record, and starts the next step while the unrecorded child continues running.

findings.title: A failed first ownership write leaves a live child without a durable block
findings.detail: When the first ownership insert fails, ownershipWriteFailed prevents the error path from killing the direct child, but no cleanup record exists. The in-memory termination error blocks only the current process scope. After a daemon restart or a later run using the checkout, recovery sees no pending record and permits work while the child remains alive. The new test explicitly verifies that the child is not killed but does not verify recovery after the write failure.
findings.suggestion: Establish a durable invocation-level cleanup intent before launching or otherwise ensure that a persistence failure leaves a durable checkout block that survives restart.
findings.failure_scenario: A transient SQLite write failure occurs on the first cleanup ownership insert while the invocation's child is running. The run fails, the daemon restarts after the database becomes writable, and a subsequent invocation starts with the old child still writing.

output.summary: Reviewed the cleanup lifecycle, persistence, startup and resume paths. The focused test command passed eight process-level cases but could not run three integration cases because @modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js was unavailable in the checkout.

findings.title: Recovery loses descendants that were not yet recorded
findings.detail: Ownership is persisted one member at a time, and recovery only visits persisted members; it never resumes discovery using the invocation marker. A crash during the initial scan, or after freezing one generation but before discovering a child forked during that scan, leaves unrecorded descendants running. Recovery deletes the partial record and permits the run to continue, even though those descendants can still write to the checkout.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough invocation-level information before cleanup begins to resume discovery and finish the freeze-and-sweep procedure after a restart, retaining the record until the entire invocation is confirmed gone.
findings.failure_scenario: A marked process forks during the first sweep and the daemon dies before the next scan records the child. Startup kills the recorded parent, deletes the record, and resumes work while the child continues running.

findings.title: A failed first ownership write leaves no recoverable cleanup
findings.detail: If the first record insertion fails, ownershipWriteFailed prevents the direct child from being killed, but no invocation-level record exists for startup or a later run to find. The process can continue writing after the run fails, and recovery has no durable indication that the checkout is unsafe.
findings.suggestion: Create a durable invocation-level cleanup record before starting the sweep and fail closed when it cannot be persisted, with a recovery path that can rediscover the invocation.
findings.failure_scenario: SQLite rejects the first ownership insertion while a tool-enabled process is running. The shutdown reports an error without signalling that child; after restart, pendingProcessCleanups is empty and the surviving child remains untracked.

findings.title: Rollback ignores unresolved cleanup records
findings.detail: The new table is additive, but the previous release has no reader for it. If the new daemon crashes during cleanup and deployment rolls back, the older daemon can resume the run without recovering or refusing the recorded processes. Those processes may be stopped indefinitely or, if not yet frozen, continue writing alongside resumed work.
findings.suggestion: Provide a rollback-compatible barrier that the previous release already respects, or explicitly prevent rollback from starting runs until pending cleanup has been resolved.
findings.failure_scenario: The new daemon records a descendant and dies before signalling it; deployment restarts the previous release, which ignores process_cleanups and resumes the checkout while the descendant is still alive.

output.summary: Reviewed the workflow, timeout helper, marker setup, and tests; found no concrete defects. The marker test passed locally. The two Linux-only timeout tests were skipped on this macOS host, so their behavior could not be verified here.

Reviewed the workflow, timeout helper, marker setup, and tests. The targeted test passed on macOS, but its two Linux-only timeout cases were skipped; GNU timeout behavior could not be checked on this host. The workflow change also carries an automated audit flag requiring an explicit workflows allowance.

findings.title: Timeout cleanup misses children in separate process groups
findings.detail: The final kill targets only the timeout process group. The suite routinely starts subprocesses with detached: true through runProcess, which puts them in separate process groups. If one of those subprocesses hangs, it survives both signals. A survivor holding the step's output pipe open can prevent the step from finishing until the outer job timeout, recreating the missing-log failure this change is meant to prevent. The helper test exercises only children in the original group.
findings.suggestion: Terminate the full descendant tree, including processes in separate groups, and exercise that case in the helper test.
findings.failure_scenario: A test invokes a detached subprocess that hangs while inheriting stdout or stderr; the 20-minute timeout kills the original group but leaves that subprocess and its output pipe alive.

output.summary: Reviewed the audit, feedback, and publication paths. The targeted test command could not run because this checkout has no node_modules and Bun could not resolve the entities package.

findings.title: Decode credential-bearing paths before redacting diagnostics
findings.detail: The new publication diagnostic applies literal credential redaction to the raw path. A percent-encoded registered credential is not matched by redactCredentials, and redactPrivate only checks the private-strings entries. The reversible encoded credential can therefore be stored or shown in the refusal message.
findings.suggestion: Decode supported path encodings before credential redaction, or replace the path with a safe placeholder whenever a decoded form contains a registered credential.
findings.failure_scenario: A file path contains a percent-encoded registered token and its content triggers a decoding-limit refusal. The resulting error includes the encoded token in the reported path.

findings.title: Warn when a file is renamed into a root hidden directory
findings.detail: The warning only examines additions. Git's rename detection reports a moved file as R rather than A, so moving an existing report into a root hidden directory produces no scratch warning even though the destination is newly introduced.
findings.suggestion: Include rename destinations when checking whether a file has been introduced beneath a root hidden directory.
findings.failure_scenario: A round moves report.xml to .tmp-gate/report.xml without changing its contents; diffSince reports R100 and the audit emits no root-hidden-addition warning.

findings.title: Match patch sections to their own paths when blob IDs coincide
findings.detail: The diagnosis associates a patch section with the first raw entry having matching old and new blob IDs. Distinct paths can share those IDs, so a decoding refusal caused by a later path can name an unrelated earlier path.
findings.suggestion: Parse the path from each patch section or preserve the ordered association between raw entries and patch sections.
findings.failure_scenario: One commit adds two empty files with identical blob IDs, and the second filename contains an over-deep percent encoding. The refusal can identify the first filename as the cause.

output.summary: Reviewed the audit, feedback, publication diagnosis, and tests. Targeted tests could not run because the checkout lacks the entities dependency.

findings.title: Large text logs with control characters do not receive the requested warning
findings.detail: The size map excludes files that fail reviewableText, which rejects escape characters and other control bytes even when Git treats the file as text. Consequently, auditDiff cannot warn about a large text log containing ANSI color sequences, a plausible form of scratch output.
findings.suggestion: Record sizes for files classified as text without requiring the stricter executable-content reviewability check.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer commits a 150 KiB UTF-8 gate log containing ANSI escape sequences as output.txt at the checkout root. Git treats it as text, but headTextSizes omits it and no large-text-addition warning is produced.

findings.title: Diagnosis cannot identify a decoding refusal in an empty file's path
findings.detail: Patch diagnosis requires an index line to associate a section with its raw path. Git omits that line for an added empty file, so a filename whose encoded text exceeds the decoding limit causes the aggregate scan to refuse publication but diagnosis falls through to the original generic error. The request explicitly requires the refusal to identify the commit and path.
findings.suggestion: Associate patch sections with raw paths even when Git emits no index line, and test an empty added file with an undecodable filename.
findings.failure_scenario: A commit adds an empty file whose name contains a percent-encoded sequence requiring more than five decoding rounds. Publication is refused as 'Published content exceeds the private text decoding limit' without the commit or path.

output.summary: Reviewed the audit and publication redaction paths and their callers. Focused probes confirmed two base64 bypasses. A publication-level probe could not run because the checkout lacks the entities dependency.

findings.title: Publication checks omit registered credentials
findings.detail: The new decoder only checks the entries supplied by its caller. Production publication callers supply private-string entries, not registered credentials, so a base64-encoded registered credential in a commit, patch, PR title, or body can pass the publication check. The filename diagnosis adds credentials separately, but that does not protect published content. Probe: `bun -e 'import { privateMatches } from "./src/gates/private.ts"; import { registerCredential, registeredCredentials } from "./src/util/proc.ts"; const secret="synthetic-secret-credential"; registerCredential("review-test",secret); const encoded=Buffer.from(secret).toString("base64"); console.log(JSON.stringify({registered:registeredCredentials().includes(secret), encoded, publicationEntries:[], matches:privateMatches(encoded,[])}));'` produced `{"registered":true,"encoded":"c3ludGhldGljLXNlY3JldC1jcmVkZW50aWFs","publicationEntries":[],"matches":[]}`.
findings.suggestion: Include registered credentials in the protected entries used at every publication boundary, and test the production callers rather than only supplying credentials explicitly in a unit test.
findings.failure_scenario: A registered API credential that is absent from private-strings.txt appears base64-encoded in an added text file and the file is published.

findings.title: URL-safe base64 breaks protected runs at hyphens and underscores
findings.detail: The base64 run expression excludes the URL-safe alphabet's `-` and `_`, splitting encoded values before they can be decoded. This bypasses both publication matching and the new audit filename and detail checks. Probe: `bun -e 'import { privateMatches } from "./src/gates/private.ts"; const s="synthetic-credential-???"; const e=Buffer.from(s).toString("base64url"); console.log(JSON.stringify({s,e,matches:privateMatches(e,[{value:s,entry:1}])}));'` produced `{"s":"synthetic-credential-???","e":"c3ludGhldGljLWNyZWRlbnRpYWwtPz8_","matches":[]}`.
findings.suggestion: Recognize and decode URL-safe base64 runs as well as the standard alphabet, with tests for both filename and published-content paths.
findings.failure_scenario: A filename or published text contains a URL-safe base64 encoding of a registered credential or private entry whose encoding contains `_` or `-`.

output.summary: Reviewed the changed redaction paths, their production callers, and the added tests. Targeted test files could not load because the checkout lacks the entities dependency; a direct matcher probe reproduced one bypass.

findings.title: Publication checks do not include registered credentials
findings.detail: The new base64 matcher only checks the entries supplied by callers. Production publication callers supply private-string entries, not registered credentials, so a base64-encoded credential in a PR body, commit, or published file passes the check. Literal credential redaction does not remove the encoded value. The added publication test constructs a combined list itself and therefore misses the production wiring.
findings.suggestion: Include registered credentials in the protected entries used by every publication check, and test through a production publication caller.
findings.failure_scenario: A registered credential is base64-encoded in a file included in a factory PR, while private-strings.txt does not contain that credential; the publication scan permits it.

findings.title: Base64 wrapping another supported encoding bypasses matching
findings.detail: A base64 run is decoded only when its immediate decoded text already contains a protected value. Consequently, the successive decoding loop never sees a base64-encoded percent escape, Unicode escape, or second base64 layer containing the protected value. This also bypasses the audit filename and detail checks. The direct probe `bun -e 'import { privateMatches } from "./src/gates/private.ts"; const value="synthetic-secret-value"; const entries=[{value,entry:1}]; const encoded=Buffer.from(Array.from(value,c=>`%${c.charCodeAt(0).toString(16)}`).join("")).toString("base64"); console.log(JSON.stringify({encoded,matches:privateMatches(encoded,entries)}));'` returned `{"encoded":"JTczJTc5JTZlJTc0JTY4JTY1JTc0JTY5JTYzJTJkJTczJTY1JTYzJTcyJTY1JTc0JTJkJTc2JTYxJTZjJTc1JTY1","matches":[]}`.
findings.suggestion: Recognize protected values after bounded successive decoding of eligible base64 runs, and cover mixed encoding layers in publication and audit tests.
findings.failure_scenario: An added filename contains base64 of the percent-encoded registered credential; the encoded filename and its detail survive into audit findings and retry feedback.

output.summary: Reviewed the changed aggregation, CLI, HTTP route, and tests. Production aggregation tests passed. CLI and HTTP tests could not run reliably because this checkout lacks the declared MCP SDK and resolves an incompatible Zod version.

findings.title: Report available cache usage for implementation evals
findings.detail: Every implementation eval records rounds, so this branch always marks its input and cache token counts unknown, even though the trial stores aggregate cache-read and cache-write counts. A single such eval also makes the provider-wide sums unknown. This leaves requested token metrics unavailable for normal implementation evals.
findings.suggestion: Use the trial-level cache totals where they can be attributed accurately, including single-round trials, and preserve known aggregate totals for multi-round trials.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementation eval completes one round with recorded input, cache-read, and cache-write usage; its provider and model statistics report all three as null.

findings.title: Do not treat eval round outcomes as invocation outcomes
findings.detail: Implementation round evidence is changed after the provider call when grading fails or times out, and its duration is extended through grading. Aggregating that evidence as an invocation therefore reports a successful provider call as failed and includes test or audit time in provider wall time.
findings.suggestion: Derive invocation success and wall time from stored provider-call evidence, or distinguish unavailable invocation measurements from round-level outcomes.
findings.failure_scenario: A provider returns successfully, then the implementation's grading command times out. The provider's successful share decreases and its wall time includes the grading timeout.

findings.title: Avoid attributing a review panel's combined usage to one provider
findings.detail: For eval trials without rounds, the code counts one trial under details.provider and assigns it the entire trial usage. Review panels can invoke multiple finders and verifiers on different providers; the runner combines their usage into the trial. The resulting counts and costs are attributed to the target provider while the other providers' work disappears.
findings.suggestion: Aggregate per-call panel evidence when available, and represent unattributable combined usage without assigning it to a single provider.
findings.failure_scenario: A review eval uses provider A for its target and provider B for a verifier. Statistics show one A invocation with both calls' cost and no B invocation.

findings.title: Apply the cutoff to each eval invocation's time
findings.detail: The query filters the whole trial by its creation time and assigns every round to that same day. Multi-round evals can cross a cutoff or midnight, so later work is excluded entirely or reported on the wrong day.
findings.suggestion: Use per-round invocation timestamps where stored; otherwise expose the limitation instead of presenting trial creation as each invocation's date.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementation trial starts before midnight and retries after midnight. A since filter for midnight omits the retry, and the daily breakdown attributes both rounds to the previous day.

output.summary: Reviewed the aggregation, CLI, HTTP route, and eval persistence paths. The workload aggregation tests passed. CLI and HTTP tests could not run successfully because this checkout has missing or incompatible installed dependencies, including the MCP SDK and Zod.

findings.title: Attribute ordinary eval trials to their provider
findings.detail: Ordinary eval trials do not populate details.provider, and only hidden implementation cases persist round records. Consequently, completed triage, spec, review, and other non-hidden evals are placed under the unknown provider even though their model target was selected by the runner. The provider breakdown therefore omits normal eval work.
findings.suggestion: Resolve provider attribution from durable trial evidence or persist the resolved provider when the invocation is recorded, with compatibility handling for existing trials.
findings.failure_scenario: A completed triage eval for a configured provider has details.invocationStatus and token totals but no details.provider or details.rounds; its entire workload appears under (unknown).

findings.title: Preserve available cache totals for eval rounds
findings.detail: Every trial with round evidence forces both cached-token fields to null, even when the trial stores aggregate cacheReadTokens and cacheWriteTokens. Since summarize propagates any null to the whole sum, a single implementation eval makes those fields unknown for its provider, model, role, and day. The requested cached-token statistics are thus unavailable for normal implementation evals despite the stored trial totals.
findings.suggestion: Use the stored trial cache totals wherever they can be attributed without fabrication, including single-round trials and provider-level aggregates for same-provider rounds.
findings.failure_scenario: A one-round implementation eval records 100 cache-read tokens in details.cacheReadTokens and one round; the eval workload reports null cache-read tokens instead of 100.

findings.title: Calculate eval success from invocation outcomes
findings.detail: Round status is not always the provider invocation status: the eval runner can replace it with an implementation grader's error or timeout after a successful model call. Counting that status as an invocation failure makes the requested successful share depend on grading and gate outcomes rather than provider execution.
findings.suggestion: Use separately recorded invocation outcomes for the successful share, and represent unavailable outcomes explicitly when older round records cannot distinguish them.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementation model returns successfully but its graded execution times out; the stored round status becomes timeout and the provider's successful share reports the invocation as failed.

findings.title: Do not attribute combined panel work to a single provider
findings.detail: For non-hidden review systems, trial totals can combine calls to multiple finders and verifiers, but this code represents the whole trial as one invocation with one model and at most one provider. This undercounts invocations and cannot provide correct per-provider or per-model costs and tokens for panel evals.
findings.suggestion: Aggregate individual recorded call evidence where available; otherwise expose the combined work as unattributed rather than presenting it as one provider invocation.
findings.failure_scenario: A panel review invokes two finder models and a verifier on different providers; the output reports one unknown-provider trial with their combined usage rather than three provider/model workloads.

output.summary: Reviewed the changed classifier, rerun resolution, redaction, and tests. Targeted tests could not load because the checkout lacks the entities dependency. A direct probe found a credential-redaction regression.

findings.title: Windowed redaction exposes short credentials used as image values
findings.detail: Short registered credentials are redacted only when the entire input to redactCredentials equals the credential. publication now passes surrounding log text as well as the selected image value, so that equality no longer holds. The resulting image and signature can be stored with the credential unredacted. A direct probe using `registerCredential("REVIEW_SHORT", "abc123")` and `ciSignature("test", "Image: abc123\n(fail) broken", "failure")` returned `"image":"abc123"` and a signature containing `abc123`; the previous implementation redacted the extracted image value.
findings.suggestion: Preserve exact-value redaction for the selected window while retaining surrounding context for credentials crossing its boundaries.
findings.failure_scenario: A registered credential shorter than eight characters is exactly the value of an Image line in a CI log. The classifier persists that value in the CI failure image and signature.

output.summary: Reviewed the changed signature, excerpt, redaction, and rerun-resolution paths. Targeted tests could not load because the checkout is missing the entities dependency. An isolated probe confirmed an excerpt boundary defect.

findings.title: Long failing test names disappear from the excerpt
findings.detail:
When a Bun assertion block precedes a failing test line longer than the remaining excerpt budget, the tail window keeps only the end of that line. The signature contains the beginning of the test name, but the excerpt contains neither the `(fail)` marker nor that beginning. The isolated command `bun -e 'import {ciSignature} from "./src/integrations/ci-classifier.ts"; const r=ciSignature("test", "error: assertion failed
stack
(fail) " + "x".repeat(3000), "fallback"); console.log(JSON.stringify({line:r.line.slice(0,30),excerptLength:r.excerpt.length,hasFail:r.excerpt.includes("(fail)"),excerptStart:r.excerpt.slice(0,50)}));'` produced `{"line":"(fail) xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx","excerptLength":1999,"hasFail":false,"excerptStart":"error: assertion failed
xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"}`.
findings.suggestion: Reserve space for the beginning of the selected signature line when bounding the tail, then use the remaining space for nearby diagnostic context.
findings.failure_scenario: A Bun assertion is followed by a failing test whose name exceeds the excerpt budget; the CI fix round receives an excerpt without the failing test marker or the start of its name.

output.summary: Reviewed the changed worker, checkout, event, and shared-runner paths. Focused tests could not start because the checkout has a missing MCP SDK dependency and an incompatible Zod installation.

findings.title: Event sequence numbers collide when a job is retried
findings.detail: Every attempt starts its sequence at zero, but the coordinator retains earlier attempts' event rows and ignores inserts that conflict on job ID and sequence. A later attempt can complete successfully while its first batches are silently discarded and the recorded events describe the failed attempt instead.
findings.suggestion: Make event sequencing or storage attempt-aware, and test a job that emits events, fails, and is leased to another worker.
findings.failure_scenario: Worker A posts sequence 0 and loses its lease; worker B retries the same job and posts its own sequence 0, which the coordinator ignores.

findings.title: A rejected event batch does not report job failure
findings.detail: A rejected post aborts the job controller. The catch block then skips the failure request because the job signal is aborted, leaving the coordinator to discover the failure only when the lease expires. This also loses the actual rejection reason.
findings.suggestion: Abort the harness on post rejection but report the failure using a separate bounded signal when the lease is still held.
findings.failure_scenario: The coordinator rejects a malformed or oversized event batch while the worker otherwise remains connected; the harness stops, but the job remains leased until expiry.

findings.title: Event batches can exceed the coordinator's request limit
findings.detail: Batching limits only the number of events, while the events endpoint rejects bodies larger than 1 MiB. A single large tool result, or several smaller results in one batch, therefore prevents an otherwise valid session from completing.
findings.suggestion: Bound serialized batches to the endpoint's limit and define how to handle an individual event that exceeds it.
findings.failure_scenario: A tool returns more than 1 MiB of output in one event; the worker posts it unchanged and the coordinator rejects the batch.

findings.title: Partition fencing can run substantially after lease expiry
findings.detail: The independent interval checks at heartbeat-sized intervals and uses a strict greater-than comparison. Depending on heartbeat and interval timing, a partitioned session can continue for nearly another heartbeat interval after one lease period has elapsed, continuing to consume model quota after the required fencing deadline.
findings.suggestion: Schedule fencing against the last successful heartbeat's exact lease deadline and reschedule it after each successful heartbeat.
findings.failure_scenario: The last heartbeat succeeds just after an interval tick, then the coordinator becomes unreachable; the next check after 60 seconds can occur almost 10 seconds late with default settings.

output.summary: Reviewed the changed worker lifecycle, shared runner, lease protocol, and tests. Targeted tests could not run because the checkout's installed dependencies are incomplete or incompatible: workers.test.ts could not find entities, and agent-test.test.ts loaded a Zod version without prefault.

findings.title: A rejected event batch aborts the job without reporting failure
findings.detail: A rejected events request aborts the job controller. The catch block then skips the failure POST because jobSignal is aborted, leaving the coordinator's job leased until its lease expires. This also loses the rejection reason and delays reassignment.
findings.suggestion: Track event-post failures separately from cancellation, abort the harness, and report failure using a signal that remains usable while the worker still owns the lease.
findings.failure_scenario: The coordinator rejects an oversized or invalid event batch with HTTP 400. The harness stops, but the job remains leased until expiry instead of immediately receiving a failure.

findings.title: Event sequence numbers restart on a retried job
findings.detail: Each worker attempt starts seq at zero, while the coordinator retains event rows keyed by job ID and sequence and silently ignores conflicts. If an earlier attempt posted batches before failing, the next attempt's batches collide with those rows and are discarded; later batches can be mixed with the previous attempt's events.
findings.suggestion: Give attempts distinct event identities or coordinate a sequence that continues across attempts, with an explicit policy for prior attempt events.
findings.failure_scenario: Worker A posts batch 0 and fails; worker B retries the same job and posts batch 0. The coordinator accepts the request but retains A's batch, so B's events are missing from the completed job.

findings.title: Fencing can occur substantially after the lease period
findings.detail: The periodic check runs at heartbeat intervals and uses a strict greater-than comparison. A heartbeat can succeed just after a check, so a partitioned agent can continue for almost an additional heartbeat interval after the lease period; an exactly aligned check can also wait for the next tick.
findings.suggestion: Schedule or reset a deadline timer on every successful heartbeat and abort agents when that deadline expires.
findings.failure_scenario: With the default 60-second lease and 10-second heartbeat interval, a partitioned agent can continue spending quota for nearly 70 seconds after the last successful heartbeat.

findings.title: Targeted agent tests use a separate fixed-size pool
findings.detail: The shared slotted-command runner creates an AgentTestSession with its default pools. Its small lane uses agentTestSlots, a separate semaphore fixed at two, rather than the worker's configured gate-slot pool. Targeted test commands therefore do not share the requested worker gate capacity.
findings.suggestion: Allow the worker's session to use its configured gate-slot pool for agent test commands while preserving coordinator behavior.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker configured for one gate slot runs a gate and two targeted agent test commands at the same time, exceeding the requested local capacity.

output.summary: Reviewed the changed restart, reconciliation, adoption, worker reporting, and test paths. The targeted test command could not run because the checkout is missing the 'entities' dependency; it reported four import errors before executing tests.

findings.title: A rejected reattachment can fall back locally after an unreported push
findings.detail: After cancelling an open job that fails a resume check, reconciliation discards its request and calls prepare(). If the coordinator worktree is dirty, prepare() returns null before checking the remote branch, so the executor runs locally even when the cancelled worker already pushed a commit without an accepted report. This bypasses the required NeedsHuman outcome and can continue work on a branch whose remote contains an unadopted worker commit.
findings.suggestion: Before falling back or replacing a cancelled open job, check the remote against that job's expected remote SHA and stop if it moved without an accepted result.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker pushes W, the coordinator restarts before accepting its report, and the coordinator worktree is dirty when the job is reconciled. The resume check fails, the job is cancelled, and prepare() returns null before inspecting the remote; a local session starts instead of ending NeedsHuman.

findings.title: Resume-check cases do not exercise the checks they name
findings.detail: The digest, HEAD, dirty-worktree, and expected-SHA cases all replace the resume hook with the same function that returns false. They test the executor's response to a rejection but never change those inputs or exercise workerPublication.resume. The explicitly requested coverage would still pass if any of those four checks were removed.
findings.suggestion: Exercise the real resume hook with each input changed independently, and assert that the old job is cancelled and a replacement is dispatched.
findings.failure_scenario: Removing the private-strings digest comparison, for example, leaves the named digest test passing because its mocked hook still returns false.

output.summary: Reviewed the worker lifecycle, restart reconciliation, adoption, grace periods, cancellation, compatibility, documentation and changed tests. The targeted test command could not run because the checkout is missing the `entities` package; no tests executed. No concrete defects were identified in the review.

The targeted Bun tests could not run because the checkout is missing the `entities` dependency; all four test files failed during module loading.

Reviewed the changed worker dispatch, result validation, refusal, fallback, restart, configuration, documentation, and tests. Targeted tests could not start because the checkout is missing the `entities` dependency.

findings.title: Local panel finders can be dispatched to workers
findings.detail: Eligibility checks the target’s harness and credential-bearing fields but does not preserve whether the review call belongs to a local finder. Local finders are routed with `billing: "free_only"`, and the catalog permits a free provider using the Claude or Codex CLI. Such a target passes this eligibility check and runs on a worker, contrary to the explicit requirement that local finders stay local.
findings.suggestion: Carry the local-finder designation through the review call and exclude it from worker eligibility; add a test using a free CLI target.
findings.failure_scenario: A panel has `local = true` for a finder whose configured free provider uses `claude-cli`, and review workers are enabled for the repository. The finder creates a worker job instead of running locally.

output.summary: Reviewed the generator, replay grading path, documentation, and tests. The targeted test could not start because the checkout lacks the entities dependency. A standalone Bun path-selection probe passed.

findings.title: Generator cannot run from this checkout because the dataset is absent
findings.detail: The default path resolves to evals/implement/cases.json, but neither that file nor its parent directory exists in the reviewed tree. The unconditional read fails before any PR is processed, so the documented CLI cannot generate a first case. The tests hide this by creating a separate dataset fixture.
findings.suggestion: Provide the required dataset or initialize a valid implement envelope when the default dataset is absent, consistent with the intended dataset ownership.
findings.failure_scenario: Run the documented generator command in a fresh checkout of this commit: readFileSync throws ENOENT for evals/implement/cases.json.

findings.title: CLI never retrieves available production complexity
findings.detail: The command-line entry point does not provide lookupRun, so every generated case receives medium even when its factory run and triage complexity are available locally. This loses the production difficulty signal the request explicitly requires; the injectable lookup is only exercised by programmatic test callers.
findings.suggestion: Wire a read-only production run lookup into the CLI and retain the fallback only when the record or complexity is unavailable.
findings.failure_scenario: Generate a case for a factory PR whose run record has small complexity: the case is persisted as medium with a lookup-not-configured note.

findings.title: Interrupted publication permanently blocks the next case ID
findings.detail: Hidden files are written before the case envelope is atomically replaced. If the process is interrupted in that interval, the orphaned hidden directory remains while cases.json still has the old highest ID. Every subsequent invocation selects the same ID and refuses it because the destination exists.
findings.suggestion: Stage hidden files in a temporary directory and provide recovery for an orphaned destination before publishing the case.
findings.failure_scenario: The generator is terminated after creating hidden/impl-013 but before renaming cases.json; rerunning any PR repeatedly reports that impl-013 already exists and cannot add cases.

output.summary: The generator cannot run against this checkout because the implement dataset is absent, and its CLI never looks up available production complexity. The targeted replay test could not run because the entities dependency is not installed.

findings.title: Generator requires a dataset that is absent from the repository
findings.detail: The generator immediately reads evals/implement/cases.json, but this checkout contains no evals/implement directory or cases.json. The documented command therefore fails before it can inspect a PR or create a case. The new tests use a separately created temporary dataset, so they do not exercise the default path.
findings.suggestion: Provide the existing implement dataset at the runner's default path or otherwise ensure the generator can initialize and populate the dataset that the runner reads.
findings.failure_scenario: Running the documented generator command from a fresh checkout fails with ENOENT when it reads the default cases.json.

findings.title: CLI never retrieves available production complexity
findings.detail: The only complexity lookup is an optional injected dependency, but the actual CLI does not supply it. Consequently every case generated by the requested command receives medium even when its production run and triage complexity are available. This also lets runs with unsupported large complexity through instead of handling their actual value.
findings.suggestion: Wire the CLI to a read-only production run lookup and use the recorded triage complexity when available.
findings.failure_scenario: A merged PR has a run footer naming a locally stored run whose complexity is small; the CLI records medium and routes later evals using the wrong complexity.

findings.title: Review invocation count is reported as review rounds
findings.detail: When panel ordinals are absent, the code counts every review invocation in the Work log as a round. Retries and multiple review invocations in one round produce multiple rows, so the recorded difficulty signal can overstate the actual rounds taken.
findings.suggestion: Derive rounds from a record that identifies review rounds, or leave the count unknown when the report does not establish it.
findings.failure_scenario: A single review round has a failed invocation followed by a retry; the case is tagged review-rounds:2 even though only one round occurred.

output.summary: Reviewed the generator, eval preparation and grading changes, and repository-cache handling. Targeted tests could not start because the checkout lacks the entities dependency: bun test test/implement-replay-cases.test.ts test/evals-implement-runner.test.ts reported “Cannot find package 'entities'”.

findings.title: The documented command has no dataset to open in this checkout
findings.detail: The generator unconditionally reads the default implement cases file before processing any PR, but this revision contains no evals directory or implement dataset. The documented command therefore exits with ENOENT instead of generating cases. The tests supply a separate fixture casePath, so they do not exercise the CLI's default path.
findings.suggestion: Provide a usable default dataset at the runner's expected path, or make the command initialize or obtain the dataset while preserving the existing ID sequence.
findings.failure_scenario: Run the documented command from this revision with any valid repository and PR number; reading evals/implement/cases.json fails before GitHub is queried.

findings.title: Validation retains tracked changes made by setup that grading discards
findings.detail: Validation runs setup and immediately injects and executes the hidden tests. Actual implement grading runs the gates and then resets tracked files and cleans untracked files before injecting hidden tests. Consequently, a head setup command that modifies a tracked source file can make validation pass using that modified file even though grading restores the committed version and fails. The generator can publish a case whose reference solution does not pass under the runner.
findings.suggestion: Reproduce the grading cleanup before injecting hidden files in both validation checkouts, using the same cleanup semantics as gradeImplement.
findings.failure_scenario: At head, setup rewrites a tracked source file to satisfy the hidden test, while its committed contents do not satisfy it. The generator accepts the head result, but a trial graded from that same committed tree fails after the runner resets the setup change.

findings.title: The CLI never looks up available production complexity
findings.detail: Although replayProduction supports an injected run lookup, the only documented CLI does not provide one. It therefore records every generated case as medium even when the report names a locally available production run whose triage complexity is trivial or small. This loses the requested production signal and places cases in the wrong complexity cell.
findings.suggestion: Connect the CLI to a read-only lookup of the named run record and use its complexity when available.
findings.failure_scenario: Generate a case for a factory PR whose footer identifies a stored run with complexity small; the resulting case has complexity medium and notes that lookup was not configured.

output.summary: Reviewed the generator, validation path, runner changes, Git changes, docs, and tests. Targeted tests could not start because the checkout is missing the entities dependency.

findings.title: Snapshot preparation excludes replays of this repository
findings.detail: Every generated case is forced into snapshot mode, which removes the entire evals directory. The repository's baseline typecheck and tests depend on files under that directory, including the JSON imports in src/evals/trace.ts and dataset reads in test/evals-cases.test.ts. prepareImplement rejects a snapshot when a baseline check fails, so PRs based on such revisions are excluded before their hidden tests can be validated. This defeats the requested generator for the factory's own PRs.
findings.suggestion: Provide a replay preparation approach that prevents solution contamination while retaining the repository data needed by its baseline checks, and exercise it against a representative Limitless base.
findings.failure_scenario: Generate a replay from a recent Limitless PR whose base includes the eval dataset imports: snapshot preparation removes those files, baseline checks fail, and no case is generated.

findings.title: The CLI never looks up available production complexity
findings.detail: The command-line entry point supplies no lookupRun dependency, so replayProduction always defaults complexity to medium even when the report identifies a locally persisted run whose triage complexity is available. The only implementation of the requested lookup is injectable by programmatic callers, not wired into the requested generator command.
findings.suggestion: Wire the CLI to a read-only production run lookup and preserve the recorded complexity when available.
findings.failure_scenario: A merged PR's report names a locally stored run with small triage complexity; invoking the documented generator writes medium instead.

findings.title: Validation omits gate effects present during actual grading
findings.detail: Validation runs setup and then the hidden command, but gradeImplement runs all baseline-selected gates before injecting hidden files and preserves ignored outputs from those gates. Consequently validation can accept a head that fails in the runner or reject a valid head when a check creates an ignored artifact used by the hidden test. The fresh validation checkout does not reproduce the grading state.
findings.suggestion: Run the same gate and cleanup sequence used by grading before executing hidden tests in each validation checkout.
findings.failure_scenario: A base-selected check creates an ignored generated file that changes a hidden test's result. Validation never runs that check, while actual grading does, so the recorded base/head result differs from the runner's result.

output.summary: Reviewed the snapshot, execution, reuse, retry, and evidence paths. The targeted integration test could not run because the checkout is missing the entities dependency.

findings.title: Timed-out factory executions are neither retried nor reused
findings.detail: The session path calls retryRegressions, which excludes timeouts, and completed rejects timed-out results. The gates stage therefore has no record to reuse and runs the suite again. This differs from the normal gates stage, which retries timeout-only failures, and violates the requirement to carry failures and retries through to reuse.
findings.suggestion: Apply the gates stage's timeout retry and classification behavior to the session execution, then persist and reuse its final result.
findings.failure_scenario: A full-suite request times out under normal machine load. The implementer receives a timeout, and the gates stage runs the same suite again on the unchanged tree.

findings.title: A snapshot gate can be recorded after its HEAD changes
findings.detail: The result is stored under the original tree without checking the snapshot checkout's HEAD after the gate runs. The normal gates stage explicitly checks that HEAD still matches the checked commit before producing verification evidence. A test or setup command that changes HEAD can therefore produce a passing result for a different commit, which is subsequently reused as evidence for the original tree.
findings.suggestion: Record the snapshot commit identity before execution and refuse to cache the result if HEAD no longer matches it after the gate and its retries.
findings.failure_scenario: A candidate test switches the snapshot checkout to another commit and passes there. The unchanged candidate tree is then committed, and the gates stage reuses that pass as evidence for the candidate.

output.summary: Reviewed the snapshot, execution, reuse, evidence, and worker paths. The targeted test command could not start because the checkout's installed dependencies are incomplete or incompatible: it reported a missing entities package and Zod methods including overwrite and prefault. No test assertions ran.

findings.title: Completed setup failures and timeouts are never reused
findings.detail: The record is written only when setup succeeded and the test result completed without a timeout. A setup failure or timed-out test therefore causes the gates stage to execute the same suite again on the same tree. The in-session path also does not perform the gates stage's timeout retry. This misses the requested reuse of failures and preservation of retries and classification.
findings.suggestion: Record completed gate executions including setup failures and timeout outcomes, and apply the same timeout retry and classification rules before recording them.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer requests the suite, its test check times out, and the round commits the unchanged snapshot. No record exists, so the gates stage runs the test check again.

findings.title: Record is accepted without checking whether the gate changed HEAD
findings.detail: The snapshot execution is recorded under the original tree even if setup or the test command changes the checkout's HEAD before producing its result. The normal gates stage explicitly checks HEAD before creating verification evidence, but this path does not. A reused pass can consequently become evidence for a tree the gate did not actually test.
findings.suggestion: Capture the snapshot checkout's initial commit and refuse to record its result if HEAD changes during execution, including retries.
findings.failure_scenario: A test script checks out another commit and runs its tests successfully. The result is stored against the original snapshot tree, reused after that tree is committed, and can satisfy gate substitution.

findings.title: Gate mode changes worker implementers to refusal
findings.detail: A worker implementer receiving the new gate setting is forced into refuse mode. Worker sessions were explicitly required to keep their existing behavior; for a repository previously using the default slot mode, adopting gate mode now prevents workers from running a full suite that previously ran under a slot.
findings.suggestion: Preserve worker-side slot behavior when the coordinator's setting is gate.
findings.failure_scenario: A repository changes from the default slot setting to gate while using worker implementers. A worker's full-suite command is refused instead of running in the gate lane as before.

findings.title: A source branch named snapshot overwrites the synthetic checkout HEAD
findings.detail: The new repository's HEAD points to refs/heads/snapshot, and the subsequent copy of source refs can overwrite that same ref. The files and index still contain the requested tree, but HEAD then identifies the source branch's commit instead of the synthetic snapshot commit. Git-aware checks can see an inconsistent checkout or test the wrong revision.
findings.suggestion: Use a detached HEAD or a private ref that cannot collide with copied source refs.
findings.failure_scenario: The source repository has a branch named snapshot. Copying refs overwrites the synthetic HEAD target, so git rev-parse HEAD^{tree} differs from the requested snapshot tree.

output.summary: Reviewed the changed execution, lease, restart, configuration and rollback paths. The targeted command `bun test test/gate-inplace-executor.test.ts` could not start because this checkout is missing the `entities` dependency; no test assertion was reached.

findings.title: Persisting an in-place request can store credentials unredacted
findings.detail: The entire request, including gate commands, is written to SQLite without sanitization. LAN jobs previously detect credential-bearing executable inputs and keep them local; in-place jobs explicitly bypass that protection. A registered credential embedded in a configured command is therefore stored verbatim in gate_jobs.
findings.suggestion: Keep credential-bearing requests out of durable job storage or use a design that protects the credential while still executing the original command.
findings.failure_scenario: A gate command contains a registered token and the in-place executor is enabled; enqueue writes that token into gate_jobs.request.

findings.title: Rollback leaves the executor believing the old daemon release is current
findings.detail: Release detection depends on a setting that only the new daemon writes. After rollback to the previous release, that daemon never updates the setting, so the executor continues renewing and running jobs from the newer release. The previous daemon also does not understand in-place handles or their stop protocol, so resumed work can start another gate in the same worktree while the executor's gate is still running.
findings.suggestion: Use a daemon identity and release observation that changes or expires even when the running daemon predates this feature, and ensure rollback waits for the prior job to stop before reusing its worktree.
findings.failure_scenario: Deploy the new release, start an in-place gate, then roll back while it is running. The old daemon starts without changing executor.daemonRelease, and the executor continues the gate under the stale release value.

findings.title: A live but unresponsive executor prevents fallback indefinitely
findings.detail: Executor availability is based only on PID and birth identity, not a fresh heartbeat. After its lease expires, sweep marks the job failed, but waitStopped waits as long as that process exists, even if it can no longer renew or acknowledge cancellation. Consequently the daemon never reaches the promised in-process fallback.
findings.suggestion: Track executor heartbeat freshness and provide a bounded, verified process-recovery path when an owner is alive but no longer responsive.
findings.failure_scenario: The executor process stalls while running a gate. Its lease expires, but its PID remains alive; the attaching daemon waits forever in waitStopped.

findings.title: Targeted and other retry jobs are always discarded on restart
findings.detail: Resume is limited to baseline, initial and rebase purposes. A recorded in-place targeted retry or timeout retry is cancelled even when its stage, round, SHA, environment and lease all match. This repeats work after a daemon restart despite the request explicitly requiring the targeted retry to reattach.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough retry context to resume matching retry jobs and attach to them while their lease remains valid.
findings.failure_scenario: A daemon restarts during a long regression-retry-targeted gate; the resumed stage rejects the matching handle, cancels the executor job and runs the retry again.

findings.title: Repositories falling back from LAN gates never use the enabled executor
findings.detail: When gates.executor is LAN, gateExecutorFor returns the LAN executor regardless of executorEnabled. Its start method directly selects the in-process executor for repositories absent from workers.repos, so those local gates cannot survive a daemon restart even with the in-place executor enabled.
findings.suggestion: Route the LAN executor's local fallback through the in-place executor when it is enabled and available.
findings.failure_scenario: Configure LAN gates for one repository, enable the local executor, and run a different repository. Its gates run inside the daemon and are lost on restart.

output.summary: Reviewed the changed executor, job leases, restart paths, configuration, and migration. The targeted command `bun test test/gate-inplace-executor.test.ts` could not start because the checkout lacks the `entities` dependency; it reported “Cannot find package 'entities' from 'src/gates/private.ts'.”

findings.title: Rollback does not notify the running executor of the release change
findings.detail: The executor detects a release change only through the persisted executor.daemonRelease setting. The previous release never writes that setting, so rolling back leaves the newer SHA in place and the newer executor continues leasing and running jobs. The older daemon also does not understand in-place handles or protect these worktrees from its normal recovery and gate paths.
findings.suggestion: Use a release identity that the previous release already updates, or otherwise ensure a rollback makes the executor stop before the older daemon resumes work.
findings.failure_scenario: A deploy is rolled back while an in-place gate is running. The old daemon starts without changing executor.daemonRelease; the new executor continues the gate while the old daemon resumes the run and can fail on the unknown handle or start work in the same worktree.

findings.title: Restart always cancels a running targeted retry
findings.detail: Resume is restricted to baseline, initial, and rebase purposes. A targeted regression retry has a different purpose, so a restart cancels its still-leased job and resumes the stage from the initial gate instead of attaching to the retry. This omits an explicitly requested gate purpose and can repeat a long suite.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough retry-stage state to resume the targeted retry and include its purpose in the validated resume path.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts during regression-retry-targeted while the executor and its lease remain alive. The resumed stage rejects the saved handle, cancels the retry, and starts earlier gate work again.

findings.title: Executor availability has no heartbeat or freshness check
findings.detail: Availability is determined solely by whether the recorded PID and birth time still exist. A stalled executor remains available indefinitely. Once its lease expires, waitStopped also waits indefinitely while that process exists, so the daemon cannot fall back or make progress for the worktree. The request explicitly requires a fresh heartbeat and freshness timers.
findings.suggestion: Record and check a periodically renewed executor heartbeat, and define a safe stop and recovery path when it becomes stale.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor process remains alive but its event loop stops responding during a gate. The lease expires, but waitStopped keeps polling because the PID is still alive, leaving the run stuck instead of falling back.

findings.title: Worktree exclusion is not atomic with job creation
findings.detail: The scan for existing jobs and the later enqueue happen separately. Two callers starting gates for the same worktree can both see no job, then enqueue and lease both jobs. The executor loop is sequential per process, but multiple executor processes can lease the two rows concurrently.
findings.suggestion: Make worktree ownership and job creation atomic, with a database constraint or transaction that also covers competing executors.
findings.failure_scenario: Two gate starts for the same cwd overlap before either attaches and enqueues, while two executor processes are running. Both jobs are leased and execute concurrently in the same worktree.

output.summary: Reviewed the identity provider, its callers, configuration, doctor checks, and changed tests. The targeted GitHub App test could not run because the checkout is missing the `entities` dependency.

findings.title: Allowing the key inside a checkout exposes it to agents and gates
findings.detail: The configured key path can resolve to any regular file, including one inside a repository checkout. Agents and gate commands are allowed to read that checkout, so file mode 0600 does not protect the key from processes running as the factory's user. This violates the requirement that the App key never reach an agent or gate.
